## earnings — module synthesis

_Source: `earnings/99_earnings-synthesis.md`_

# Earnings Module — NHY (Synthesis)

## Abstract

Norsk Hydro's underlying earnings trend is decelerating on the top line — trailing-twelve-month revenue is down 3.2% versus FY2025 and Q1 2026 revenue fell 11.7% year on year — even though reported and adjusted profit rebounded sharply in the latest quarter. That rebound is driven almost entirely by a Middle East supply-shock spike in the LME aluminium price, which management itself calls non-repeatable and which forward bookings already show partially unwinding. Consensus for the 22-July print was cut mechanically to match management's own guided cost bridge rather than out of independent caution, weakening the "low bar" read for profit specifically even as revenue stays beatable. The biggest risk is a Q1 2026 receivables build (days sales outstanding rose from 33.0 to 56.7) that leaves the recovery's cash backing unconfirmed. The verdict is a mixed, commodity-conditional setup, not a clean acceleration.

## 1. Earnings Verdict

- **Verdict: Mixed earnings setup**
- Earnings quality /100: 55 *(from 06 — mixed/average band; recurring "one-off" restructuring and a large, persistent reported-vs-adjusted net income gap, partly offset by decent multi-year cash conversion)*
- Consensus setup /100 (higher = more beatable): 58 *(revenue-line consensus is genuinely beatable on a 4-for-4 quarterly beat streak and a capex bar the Street has set ~6.5% above guidance; EBITDA/EPS-line consensus was cut in the last 30 days to track management's own guided cost bridge — not independent conservatism — so the "low bar" read does not extend cleanly to profit; net effect is a mixed, not clearly favorable, bar)*
- Earnings volatility /100 (higher = worse): 70 *(from 07 — the two largest, highest-confidence sensitivities, LME aluminium price and USD/NOK, are both company-disclosed, both double-digit shares of Adjusted EBITDA on a single plausible move, and both outside management's control)*
- Next-quarter setup: Favors beat *(from 05, on revenue and the mechanically-lowered EBITDA/EPS bar), but qualified — see §1A and §8*
- Biggest earnings driver (one line): The LME aluminium price — a Middle East-driven supply-shock spike (quarter-end spot USD 3,467/mt vs a FY2023–25 realized band of USD 2,218–2,573/mt) that management explicitly flags as not run-rate.
- Biggest earnings risk (one line): The Q1 2026 receivables build (days sales outstanding 33.0 → 56.7, accounts receivable +82.3% quarter on quarter against only +6.7% revenue growth) leaves the earnings recovery investors are being asked to extrapolate into FQ2 2026 without confirmed cash backing.
- Red-flag severity verdict (from `08_earnings-red-flags.md`, reported verbatim): **Material concerns** — high-severity flags present; earnings setup may be overstated or fragile.

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation

- **Strongest bear point:** TTM revenue (ended Mar-2026) is down 3.2% versus FY2025 and Q1 2026 revenue is down 11.7% year on year, while the entire margin "recovery" narrative rests on a Middle East supply-shock price spike explicitly labelled not run-rate across four upstream reports (02, 03, 05, 07) [`01_historical-financials.md` §2-3; `03_margin-drivers.md` §8].
- **Strongest bull point (steelman):** Revenue has beaten Street consensus in all four of the last four quarters, and the FQ2 2026 EBITDA/EPS bar was cut into the print (FQ2 EBITDA −9.5%, zero analysts raised FQ2 EPS in the last month) while two-thirds of Q2 primary aluminium volume is already booked at USD 3,000/mt, below the quarter-end spot of USD 3,467/mt — a real, quantifiable cushion even if the underlying price reverses [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §4-6; `05_beat-miss-setup.md` §2].
- **Single killer risk:** The Q1 2026 receivables spike (DSO 33.0 → 56.7 days, AR nearly doubling quarter on quarter) turning out to be an early cash-conversion problem rather than the "ordinary working-capital cycle" `06_earnings-quality.md` calls it — if FQ2 2026's cash-flow statement (due 22-Jul-2026) shows receivables still building while CFO stays negative, the earnings recovery the market is pricing would not be cash-backed [`08_earnings-red-flags.md`, flag #1].
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** `08_earnings-red-flags.md` documents that over half (NOK 1,600m of NOK 3,050m) of the Q1 2026 QoQ Adjusted EBITDA recovery came from an opaque "Other" bucket including a one-off internal-margin-elimination release that should not repeat, and that the largest revenue segment (Extrusions, 37.5% of FY2025 revenue) still posted a −2.2% reported EBIT margin, masked at the group level by the aluminium-price spike [`08_earnings-red-flags.md`, flags MG1, MG3].

## 2. Specialist Roll-Up

| Specialist | Verdict Line | Biggest Finding |
|---|---|---|
| earnings-data-triage | Sufficient — no hard-cap-triggering gap | Full annual filing, latest quarterly filing, two verbatim transcripts, and a complete consensus/estimates export are all present; only a full 8-quarter P&L series and a dated current-price snapshot are missing, neither triggering a hard cap |
| historical-financials | Revenue decelerating and negative on a trailing basis; margins volatile, not trending in one direction | TTM revenue (ended Mar-2026) is −3.2% vs FY2025; Q1 2026 revenue −11.7% YoY on a 40% YoY drop in the alumina price index |
| revenue-drivers | Revenue story is a commodity-price/FX story overlaid on roughly flat volumes, not organic demand growth | The LME aluminium price is the single biggest revenue driver, and its current level is a geopolitically-driven spike (Middle East/Strait of Hormuz), not a normalized run-rate |
| margin-drivers | Adjusted EBITDA margin is the right metric to track; the Q1 2026 recovery is real but concentrated in one non-run-rate driver | A USD 400/mt reversal in the LME price implies roughly NOK 6.0bn of Adjusted EBITDA downside, about 21% of FY2025 group Adjusted EBITDA |
| guidance-consensus | Bar is low, but the reason matters | FQ2 2026 EBITDA/EPS estimates were cut ~30 days before the print to track management's own guided cost bridge, while FQ2 revenue estimates stayed net-positive over the same window |
| beat-miss-setup | Setup favors beat | Two-thirds of Q2 primary aluminium volume is booked at USD 3,000/mt, below the Q1'26 quarter-end spot of USD 3,467/mt, giving revenue/price upside even before considering the bar-lowering |
| earnings-quality | Score 55/100 — mixed/average band | "Significant rationalization and closure costs" are booked as a non-recurring add-back every single year (265 → 407 → 1,795 NOK m, FY23-25) and reported net income sits 34%-180% below adjusted net income in every one of the last three years |
| earnings-sensitivity | Volatility score 70/100 (inverted, high) | The two largest, highest-confidence sensitivities — LME aluminium price and USD/NOK — are both company-disclosed, both double-digit shares of Adjusted EBITDA on a single plausible move, and both outside management's control |
| earnings-red-flags | Material concerns — high-severity flags present | 15 flags triggered (0 Critical, 5 High, 6 Medium, 4 Low); the single most dangerous is the unexplained Q1 2026 receivables spike sitting directly under the quarter the "favors beat" and margin-recovery narratives are built on |

## 3. Reconciliation

- **06_earnings-quality vs business-model 11_capital-allocation-governance on the Q1 2026 cash-flow event.** `06_earnings-quality.md` characterizes Q1 2026's negative operating cash flow (NOK (1,891)m against positive Adjusted EBITDA of NOK 8,668m) as "an ordinary working-capital cycle... not accrual manipulation." The business-model module's `11_capital-allocation-governance.md`, cross-referenced via `08_earnings-red-flags.md`, quantifies the same event more sharply: days sales outstanding nearly doubled (33.0 → 56.7 days) and accounts receivable rose 82.3% quarter on quarter against only 6.7% revenue growth, scoring it 40/100 severity and calling it "unexplained." This is not a factual disagreement — both describe the same cash-flow print — but a materiality gap. **Reconciled view (conservative default, CLAUDE.md §4):** weight the more granular, quantified business-model read. The receivables build is treated in this synthesis as an unresolved cash-quality flag, not dismissed as routine, and the earnings-quality score of 55/100 is treated as a ceiling pending the FQ2 2026 cash-flow statement (due 22-Jul-2026), per `08_earnings-red-flags.md` §5-6.
- **05_beat-miss-setup's "favors beat" verdict vs 08_earnings-red-flags' caution (flag GC1).** `05` calls the setup "favors beat" based substantially on the FQ2 2026 EBITDA/EPS bar having been cut in the 30 days before the print. `08` flags that this cut tracks management's own guided Q2 cost bridge rather than independent Street conservatism — meaning if actual costs land at the guided midpoint rather than the low end, the post-cut consensus is accurate, not conservative, and the "low bar" advantage evaporates for EBITDA/EPS specifically. **Reconciled view:** "favors beat" is retained for the revenue line (a real, repeatable 4-for-4 beat streak) but downgraded to a coin-flip characterization for EBITDA/EPS, consistent with the historical pattern in that line (+15.1%, −12.8%, −6.8%, +34.4% surprise over the last four quarters).
- **00_earnings-data-triage vs 04_guidance-consensus on the consensus data-as-of date.** `00` dated the consensus data "Apr-29-2026." `04` corrected this to 2026-07-15, showing the Apr-29 timestamp belonged to the transcript's own auto-generated cover page, not the live, continuously-updated Consensus/Trends/Revisions tabs. **Reconciled view:** 04's correction is used throughout this synthesis; the consensus data is current (three days before the 22-Jul-2026 print), not stale.
- **CIQ vendor EBITDA/EBIT reclassification vs the company's own audited EBITDA/EBIT.** `01_historical-financials.md` found the CIQ workbook's EBITDA/EBIT fields do not reconcile to the audited figures (a ~NOK 27bn gap on FY2025 EBITDA) and used the company's own audited figures throughout instead. This synthesis follows that same resolution — every EBITDA/EBIT figure cited here is the company's own audited/APM figure, never the CIQ reclassification.

## 4. Score Cap Application

| Cap Trigger | Applied? (Y/N) | Affected Score | Final Cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| No consensus / estimate data | N — a full consensus/estimates export (Consensus, Trends, Revisions, Surprise, Guidance tabs) is present and current as of 2026-07-15 | Consensus setup | Not capped (max 30 not applied) |
| No cash flow statement | N — full FY2021-2025 and Q1 2026 cash flow statements are present | Earnings quality | Not capped (max 45 not applied) |
| No revision history | N — Revisions and Trends tabs give up/down revision counts and multi-window snapshots | Consensus setup | Not capped (max 60 not applied) |
| No verbatim transcript AND no sell-side proxy | N — two verbatim CIQ/S&P Global Market Intelligence transcripts (FQ4 2025, FQ1 2026) are present | Earnings clarity | Not capped (max 70 not applied) |
| Transcript role filled ONLY by a sell-side proxy (no verbatim) | N — verbatim transcripts satisfy this role directly | Earnings clarity | Not applicable |
| Only inferred sensitivities | Partial — N for the overall volatility score (the two highest-ranked, highest-magnitude variables, LME price and USD/NOK, are both company-disclosed, High confidence); Y for three lower-ranked rows individually (alumina price: Low confidence, per-unit rate inferred; extrusions volume: Medium; recycling spread: Medium) | Earnings volatility confidence | Overall score confidence remains Medium-High per `07_earnings-sensitivity.md` §7; the alumina-price row specifically carries Low confidence and should not be over-weighted in isolation |

No hard quarterly-data cap applies to Earnings clarity: the triage explicitly found the latest quarterly filing plus two transcripts satisfy the module's sufficiency bar, though a clean 8-quarter series could not be assembled from a single export — a soft precision limitation on QoQ/YoY trend reads, not a scoring cap, per `00_earnings-data-triage.md` §6 and `08_earnings-red-flags.md` flag #11.

## 5. Earnings Setup Summary

### Revenue Setup

The current revenue trajectory is not sustainable as a run-rate in either direction shown over the past year. The FY2025 growth of +2.1% and the sharp Q1 2026 rebound in profit both sit on top of a top line that is trailing-twelve-month negative (−3.2%) and fell 11.7% year on year in the latest quarter — the decline is driven almost entirely by a 41% year-on-year collapse in the realized alumina price, a structural oversupply story (2.7–3.0 million tonne 2026 global surplus) that is not obviously reversible on a short horizon. The single factor that would flip revenue direction is the LME aluminium price holding or extending its current Middle East-driven spike long enough to outrun the alumina drag and the stronger krone — but the company's own forward booking data (two-thirds of Q2 volume locked at USD 3,000/mt, below the USD 3,467/mt quarter-end spot) shows the market itself pricing some reversal already. Reported revenue and underlying organic revenue tell materially different stories: end-market demand growth is running near +1% globally while realized aluminium prices moved +21.6% year on year — the gap between the price-driven headline and the roughly flat-volume underlying business is on the order of 20 percentage points.

### Margin Setup

Current margins are not at a sustainable level in either direction — Q1 2026's Adjusted EBITDA margin of 17.20% is a cyclical peak within the visible window, up from an 11.83% trough just one quarter earlier, and the swing is dominated by a single non-run-rate driver (the LME price spike) rather than a structural improvement. If the aluminium price reverses by even USD 400/mt toward its pre-shock range, Aluminium Metal — the segment contributing 39.5% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA — takes the largest single bite, roughly NOK 6.0bn, about 21% of FY2025 group Adjusted EBITDA. Hydro has no contractual margin-protection mechanism against this: it is a price-taker on both alumina (its main input, priced with a one-month index lag) and LME aluminium (its main output, realized with a 1.5-2 month lag), and its only levers are forward hedging — which dampens but does not eliminate the swing — and its position on the low end of the industry cost curve. The improvement program (NOK 6.5bn cumulative cost-out target by 2030, NOK 1.4bn realized to date) is the one durable, self-help offset, worth roughly 50 basis points of margin per year if delivered at the disclosed pace, but it is small relative to the commodity-price swings described above.

### Quality Check

The single largest gap between reported and economic earnings is the net income/EPS line, where reported figures sat 34% (FY2025), 84% (FY2024), and 180% (FY2023) below the company's own adjusted figures every year, driven by non-cash derivative timing, impairments, and a restructuring charge that recurs every year despite being labelled one-off (265 → 407 → 1,795 NOK million, FY2023-2025) — a widening, not narrowing, gap. These add-backs are not genuinely one-time: the rationalization charge has appeared in all three disclosed years and is growing, and the derivative mark-to-market swing is a structural feature of Hydro's hedge accounting that will recur every year the metal-price path moves. To model normalized earnings for next year, start from adjusted EBITDA/EPS rather than GAAP, since GAAP is dominated by non-operating derivative timing noise — but haircut the adjusted figure modestly for the recurring rationalization add-back, which the company's own disclosure pattern suggests understates the ongoing cash cost of running an aging asset base.

### Consensus Bar

For Hydro to beat the current bar by a material margin, the unbooked third of Q2 aluminium volume would need to realize near the quarter-end spot of USD 3,467/mt rather than reverting toward the booked USD 3,000/mt, or capex would need to land at management's guided NOK 13,500m rather than the Street's higher NOK 14,377m model — both plausible, evidenced paths, not speculative ones. The bar is most likely set correctly, not too low, on the profit line specifically: the recent EBITDA/EPS estimate cuts track management's own guided cost bridge (energy, carbon, fixed-cost seasonality) rather than reflecting independent Street caution, so the "low bar" read applies more to revenue (where the cut was not made) than to EBITDA/EPS. A meaningful share of the current consensus recovery is anchored to the Middle East supply shock and its knock-on effects on recycling spreads — both explicitly flagged by management as non-durable and already partially priced out in forward bookings.

## 5b. Leverage & Capital Structure

Leverage is within normal range and did not change materially during the period — no dedicated treatment required. Adjusted net debt/Adjusted EBITDA was 0.7x at FY2025 (up from 0.2x at FY2022, down from 0.9x at FY2024), comfortably inside the company's own sub-2x target throughout the visible window, and neither the absolute-leverage trigger (>3.0x) nor the leverage-change trigger (>1.0x YoY ratio increase, >50% total-debt increase, or >2x absolute net-debt change) is met on the data available [`01_historical-financials.md` §1, footnote 5]. Net debt did rise from NOK 9,669m (FY2025) to NOK 12,860m (Q1 2026, +33.0%), a point-in-time balance-sheet move tied to the same operating-capital build discussed in §1A and §8, but this falls short of the >2x absolute-change trigger and leverage remains a secondary consideration for this module, not a standing constraint on capital allocation.

## 6. Key Numbers

- Revenue growth rate: FY2025 +2.1% YoY; TTM (ended Mar-2026) −3.2% vs FY2025; Q1 2026 −11.7% YoY [`01_historical-financials.md` §1-2]
- EBITDA margin: FY2025 reported 12.36%; Adjusted EBITDA margin 17.20% (Q1'26) vs 11.83% (Q4'25 trough) [`01_historical-financials.md` §1, §3]
- EPS: FY2025 reported diluted NOK 3.41, Adjusted NOK 5.02; Q1 2026 reported NOK 2.16, Adjusted NOK 2.07 [`01_historical-financials.md` §1, §3]
- CFO / EBITDA: 3-year average 81.3%, TTM (Mar-2026) 79.4%; Q1 2026 standalone CFO was negative NOK (1,891)m against positive Adjusted EBITDA of NOK 8,668m [`06_earnings-quality.md` §1-2]
- Biggest driver current level: LME aluminium price, 3-month average USD 3,192/mt (Q1'26), quarter-end spot USD 3,467/mt, versus a FY2023-25 realized band of USD 2,218-2,573/mt [`02_revenue-drivers.md` §7; `03_margin-drivers.md` §8]
- Consensus gap (capex, the only clean guidance-vs-consensus line): Street models NOK 14,377.4m FY2026 capex vs management's guided NOK 13,500m, a 6.5% higher Street model [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §3]
- Estimate revision direction: FY2026/FQ2 2026 EBITDA and EPS cut 4-9.5% in the 30 days before the print; FQ2 2026 revenue estimates stayed net-positive over the same window [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §4-5]
- Earnings volatility score: 70/100 (inverted — higher = worse), Medium-High confidence overall [`07_earnings-sensitivity.md` §7]

## 7. What Would Change The Earnings Verdict?

| Current Verdict | What Would Upgrade It | What Would Downgrade It | Data Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mixed earnings setup | FQ2 2026 cash-flow statement shows receivables normalizing and CFO turning positive again, AND the LME aluminium price holds near or above USD 3,000/mt through Q3 without a demand-side (non-shock) explanation emerging, AND Extrusions' reported EBIT margin turns positive | FQ2 2026 receivables keep building while CFO stays negative (confirming a genuine cash-conversion problem, not a one-quarter working-capital timing event); OR the LME price reverts toward the pre-shock USD 2,995-2,300/mt range faster than the booking data assumes, pulling the unbooked ~33% of Q2 volume down with it; OR the recurring rationalization charge grows again in FY2026, further widening the reported-vs-adjusted gap | FQ2 2026 quarterly filing and cash-flow statement (due 22-Jul-2026); confirmation or explanation of the Q1 2026 receivables spike and the unexplained 55.7% YoY Norway revenue jump; a Q3 2026 segment cost/price bridge once management issues one |

## 8. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- Dominant earnings trend: revenue is decelerating and trailing-twelve-month negative (−3.2%), while the latest quarter's profit rebound is a cyclical, non-run-rate spike tied to a Middle East supply shock in the LME aluminium price — the two trends point in different directions and neither should be extrapolated on its own.
- Earnings are not cleanly cash-backed in the most recent quarter: a large, unexplained receivables build (DSO 33.0 → 56.7 days) sits directly under the base quarter the "favors beat" thesis depends on, and this synthesis treats the 55/100 earnings-quality score as a ceiling pending the FQ2 2026 cash-flow statement, not a settled read.
- The consensus bar is not uniformly low: it is genuinely beatable on revenue (a real 4-for-4 streak) and on capex (Street models more spend than guided), but the EBITDA/EPS bar was mechanically lowered to match management's own guided cost bridge rather than out of independent Street caution — do not treat "favors beat" as applying equally across the P&L.
- Next-quarter setup favors beat on revenue and on the capex line; is closer to a coin flip on EBITDA/EPS given the historical surprise pattern (+15.1%, −12.8%, −6.8%, +34.4%) and the bar-lowering caveat above. Visibility drops materially beyond FQ2 2026 — no comparable cost/price bridge exists for Q3, and the two known structural headwinds (alumina oversupply, Extrusions demand) skew toward persistence rather than resolution within one quarter.
- Top sensitivity variable: the LME aluminium price, currently a tailwind but explicitly a one-time geopolitical spike that could reverse if the Middle East conflict resolves or curtailed Gulf/Chinese supply returns — a USD 400/mt reversal implies roughly NOK 6.0bn of Adjusted EBITDA downside, about 21% of FY2025 group Adjusted EBITDA.
- No hard partial-data caps applied in this module (consensus, cash flow, transcripts, and revision history are all present); the only soft limitation is an incomplete 8-quarter P&L series (several Q2/Q3 2025 figures are chart-derived or vendor-only, not filing-sourced), which limits trend/seasonality precision but did not trigger a scoring cap.
- Biggest missing data point: an explanation for the Q1 2026 receivables spike and for the unexplained 55.7% YoY jump in Norway revenue — neither is addressed anywhere in this data pool, and both bear directly on whether the current earnings recovery is genuine.
- Red-flag severity verdict (`08_earnings-red-flags.md`, reported verbatim): **Material concerns** — 15 flags triggered (0 Critical, 5 High, 6 Medium, 4 Low). The five High-severity flags: (1) the Q1 2026 receivables spike; (2) over half of the Q1 2026 QoQ Adjusted EBITDA recovery explained by an opaque "Other" bucket including a one-off internal-margin release; (3) the recurring "one-off" restructuring charge plus large non-cash FV/MTM swings driving a 34%-180% reported-vs-adjusted net income gap; (4) the FQ2 2026 EBITDA/EPS bar cut tracking guided costs, not independent conservatism; (5) the "favors beat" framing risk of being read as structural acceleration despite TTM revenue being negative and the recovery resting on a one-time geopolitical price shock. All five are surfaced above in §1A, §3, or §8; none are omitted.
- What would change the verdict: see §7 — the decisive near-term evidence is the FQ2 2026 cash-flow statement (due 22-Jul-2026, three days after this report's as-of date).

## 9. Simple Summary

- Revenue is shrinking on a trailing basis (−3.2% TTM, −11.7% in the latest quarter) even though the headline commodity price is spiking — the driver is price and currency, not more demand.
- Margins swung from an 11.8% trough to a 17.2% peak in one quarter, almost entirely because of a Middle East-driven aluminium price spike management itself says will not last.
- Earnings are not fully clean: a "one-off" restructuring charge shows up every single year and keeps growing, and reported profit has run 34%-180% below the company's own adjusted profit figure in each of the last three years.
- The market's bar is easy to beat on revenue and on spending (capex), but was cut to match management's own guided cost bridge on profit — so "easy to beat" does not apply evenly across the numbers.
- Next quarter (results due 22-Jul-2026) probably beats on revenue; profit is closer to a coin flip given the mixed history and the bar-lowering caveat.
- The single biggest swing factor is the aluminium price — a further USD 400/mt reversal would erase about a fifth of last year's adjusted profit.
- Earnings volatility is high (70/100, worse than most) because the two biggest levers — the aluminium price and the Norwegian krone — are both outside management's control.
- This module is useful for the final synthesizer: it identifies a real near-term catalyst (FQ2 2026 results, three days out) and a specific, checkable risk (the receivables build) that will resolve in either direction very soon.

# Historical Financials — NHY

Norsk Hydro ASA (Oslo Børs: NHY) reports under IFRS Accounting Standards as adopted by the EU, in Norwegian Krone (NOK millions), fiscal year ending 31 December [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.140]. All figures below are NOK million unless stated as per-share (NOK). This is not a US SEC or India SEBI-LODR filer; the local-equivalent documents are the Board-approved Quarterly Report (10-Q/6-K equivalent) and the Integrated Annual Report (10-K equivalent) [00_earnings-data-triage.md].

**Data-quality note on this report (read before the tables):** Norsk Hydro's audited income statement uses an IFRS "nature of expense" format with no Cost-of-Goods-Sold or Gross Profit subtotal, and no EBITDA/EBIT subtotal that matches the CIQ workbook's own "Operating Income" reclassification. A direct check found the CIQ Financials.xls Income Statement tab's "EBITDA" and "EBIT" fields (e.g., FY2025 EBITDA 51,454; EBIT 41,218) do **not** reconcile to the company's own audited/disclosed "Earnings before financial items and tax (EBIT)" and reported EBITDA (FY2025: EBIT 14,401; EBITDA 25,696) [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.140 (EBIT); p.36, "Other performance measures" table (EBITDA)]. The gap (~NOK 27bn) tracks almost exactly to a large recurring "Other Non-Operating Inc.(Exp.)" line embedded in CIQ's reclassification that has no counterpart of that size in the audited statement — this looks like a CIQ template/extraction mismatch for Hydro's income-statement structure, not a real economic item. Per CLAUDE.md §4/§5 (audited filing beats vendor; cite the source a number actually came from), this report uses the **company's own reported EBITDA/EBIT** wherever available (FY2023–FY2025, and the two quarterly filings) and does **not** use CIQ's EBITDA/EBIT fields at all. Revenue, Net Income, diluted EPS, CFO, and Capex from the CIQ Financials.xls workbook were spot-checked against the audited FY2025/FY2024 statements and matched exactly, so those lines are used as sourced. Gross Profit/Gross Margin is a CIQ reclassification (Revenue less "Raw material and energy expense") with no company-disclosed counterpart; it is retained but flagged as vendor-derived, cross-checked to the filing for FY2024–FY2025 only (COGS component matched exactly for those two years) [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.36, Note 5.3].

Company target: average Adjusted net debt/Adjusted EBITDA below 2x, with Adjusted net debt of around NOK 25bn over the cycle [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.35 and p.180].

## 2. TTM Snapshot

Latest TTM = trailing four quarters ended 31-Mar-2026 (Q2'25 + Q3'25 + Q4'25 + Q1'26, derived as FY2025 − Q1'25 + Q1'26 using company-reported figures). Prior TTM = the most recent full-year trailing-12-month window available, ended 31-Dec-2025 (i.e., FY2025 itself). A year-ago TTM (ended 31-Mar-2025) cannot be computed from this pool because standalone Q1 2024 figures are not available — this pool contains only the Q1 2026 quarterly filing plus the FY2025 annual report and two transcripts (Q4'25, Q1'26 calls), so quarters before Q1'25 are not individually broken out [00_earnings-data-triage.md, §4].

**Reported vs company "Free cash flow" APM:** Hydro's own Free cash flow APM (net cash from operating activities less net cash used in investing activities, adjusted to exclude short-term-investment purchases) was NOK **13,034 million for FY2025** and **NOK (3,985) million (negative) for Q1 2026**, per the company's own disclosure [first-quarter-report-2026.pdf, p.24, "Free cash flow" APM table]. This differs from the module-standard FCF definition used in this report's tables (CFO − total capex, no adjustment for short-term investment purchases) — FY2025 module-standard FCF is NOK 11,729 million (see §1), and the two do not agree because the company's version nets out short-term investment activity that this report's CFO/Capex definition does not. Both are shown so the two bases are not conflated.

This is because Q1 2026 adjusting items included a large unrealized derivative *loss* reversal (which lifts adjusted EBITDA/EBIT versus reported) combined with an offsetting net foreign-exchange gain and calculated tax effect that pull adjusted net income *below* reported net income for this specific quarter [first-quarter-report-2026.pdf, p.7, "Adjusting items to EBITDA, EBIT and net income" table]. Flagged here as a genuine one-off quarter dynamic for `06_earnings-quality` to examine, not an error.

## 4. Reported vs Adjusted Metrics

Company does disclose adjusted metrics as Alternative Performance Measures (APMs), reconciled in both the annual report and each quarterly report.

| EBIT | 14,401 | 18,663 | +4,262 | As above, plus impairment charges (+1,069) | [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.36] |
| EPS (diluted) | 3.41 | 5.02 | +1.61 | Adjusted net income excludes the above items net of tax; adjusted net income NOK 11,155m vs reported NOK 8,304m | [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.36 and p.64] |

| Metric | FY2024 Reported | FY2024 Adjusted | Adjustment Amount | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| EBITDA | 26,543 | 26,318 | −225 | [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.36] |
| EBIT | 16,487 | 16,284 | −203 | [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.36] |
| EPS (diluted) | 2.90 | 4.50 | +1.60 | [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.36 and p.64] |

| Metric | FY2023 Reported | FY2023 Adjusted | Adjustment Amount | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| EBITDA | 23,291 | 22,258 | −1,033 | [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.36] |

| EPS (diluted) | 1.77 | 4.26 | +2.49 | [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.36 and p.64] |

Note the sign flips year to year (FY2023/FY2024 adjustments to EBITDA are *negative* — reported exceeded adjusted — while FY2025's is positive): the adjusting items are dominated by unrealized, non-cash derivative mark-to-market swings on LME-linked contracts, which move both directions depending on the metal-price path in a given year. This is a structural feature of Hydro's earnings (heavy use of LME-linked pricing and hedging), not a one-off. `06_earnings-quality` should treat the size and direction-volatility of this adjustment as a standing signal, not a discrete event.

## 5. Quarterly Seasonality Table (last 3 fiscal years)

*Insufficient quarterly history for seasonality analysis.* This pool contains full-year figures for FY2023–FY2025 and only 5 individual quarters (Q1 2025–Q1 2026, several of them approximate — see §3). Building a 3-fiscal-year, 4-quarter-each seasonality table would require FY2023 and FY2024 quarterly filings, which are not in this pool. No quarter can be flagged as structurally >30% or <20% of annual revenue from the data available; do not infer seasonality from the 5-quarter window in §3, which spans a period of falling alumina and aluminium prices rather than a repeatable seasonal pattern [see nhy-presentation-q1-2026.pdf, p.10, PAX/alumina price commentary].

## 6. Key Trend Summary

Revenue growth is **decelerating and has turned negative on a trailing basis**: FY2022's +38.9% commodity-price spike gave way to a −6.9% FY2023 correction, only modest +5.2%/+2.1% growth in FY2024/FY2025, and the latest TTM (ended Mar-2026) is down −3.2% versus FY2025, with Q1 2026 revenue down −11.7% year-on-year on a 40% year-on-year drop in the alumina price index (PAX) [first-quarter-report-2026.pdf, p.9]. Margins are **volatile rather than trending in one direction**: reported EBITDA margin bounced between 12.0% (FY2023) and 13.0% (FY2024) before easing to 12.4% (FY2025) on a company-reported basis, while adjusted EBITDA margin on a quarterly view fell from 16.7% (Q1'25) to a trough of 11.8% (Q4'25) before rebounding to 17.2% (Q1'26) — a swing driven substantially by non-cash unrealized-derivative adjustments rather than a steady operating trend (§4). There is **no seasonality read available** from this pool (§5) — the quarter-to-quarter swings visible in §3 track commodity-price and FX moves, not a repeatable calendar pattern. The clearest **inflection point** is Q4 2025: reported EBITDA fell to NOK 1,974 million (a 4.2% margin, the weakest point in the visible window) on a large unrealized LME-derivative timing loss, before both reported and adjusted metrics recovered sharply in Q1 2026 (adjusted EBITDA +55% QoQ, adjusted EPS +196% QoQ) — company commentary attributes the Q1 2026 rebound to higher all-in aluminium prices, higher alumina and metal sales volumes, and stronger Metal Markets/Extrusions results, partly offset by lower alumina prices, a stronger NOK, and reduced power production [first-quarter-report-2026.pdf, p.5]. Net debt on the company's own APM basis has also inflected twice in the visible window — rising from NOK 8.2bn (FY2023) to NOK 16.0bn (FY2024), falling back to NOK 9.7bn (FY2025), then rising again to NOK 12.9bn at Q1 2026 on operating-capital build — leverage (Adjusted net debt/Adjusted EBITDA) stayed within the company's own sub-2x target throughout at 0.2x–0.9x (§1, footnote 5).

## earnings / 02_revenue-drivers.md

_Source: `earnings/02_revenue-drivers.md`_

# Revenue Drivers — NHY

## 1. Segment Decomposition Status

Segment decomposition applied — 5 operating segments (Bauxite & Alumina, Energy, Aluminium Metal, Metal Markets, Extrusions) plus an immaterial "Other and eliminations" bucket, from the business-model module [`analyses/NHY_2026-07-19/business-model/03_segment-map.md`]. No segment exceeds 85% of revenue or profit — Hydro is a genuinely integrated value chain, not a single-segment business. Revenue is concentrated downstream (Extrusions 37.5%, Metal Markets 36.4% of FY2025 external revenue) while profit is concentrated upstream (Aluminium Metal 39.5% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA, a company-defined measure of segment profit before financing costs, tax, depreciation and amortization, adjusted for one-off items) — a classic upstream-margin, downstream-volume pattern for an integrated aluminium producer [`03_segment-map.md`, §1-2].

## 2. Revenue Driver Tree

| Business Type | Revenue Formula |
|---|---|
| Commodity producer | Production × realized commodity price |

Hydro does not fit one line of the standard template cleanly — it is a multi-segment integrated producer where revenue in each segment is driven differently. Company-specific formula, stated as a sum of segment drivers:

**Group revenue ≈ (Alumina volume × alumina-index price) + (Primary aluminium volume × [LME price + regional premium] × USD/NOK rate) + (Extrusion volume × extrusion selling price, itself LME-linked plus a conversion margin) + (Metal Markets trading/recycling volume × spread over LME), net of intercompany eliminations.**

The common thread across all five segments is that selling prices are directly or contractually tied to the US-dollar LME aluminium price (or, for alumina, an index price with a one-month lag that is itself correlated with the aluminium cycle) [`03_segment-map.md`, row 1: "the majority of alumina Hydro sells externally is contractually linked to either the LME prices or alumina index with one-month delay" — company language paraphrased in the segment map, sourced to FY2025 Integrated Annual Report, Note 1.4], then converted into NOK, the reporting currency, at the prevailing USD/NOK rate. This means the USD/NOK exchange rate is not a peripheral translation adjustment for Hydro — it is baked into how almost every segment's selling price becomes a NOK revenue line.

## 3. Market / Share / Price / Mix Split

| Driver Bucket | Current Direction | Evidence | Importance /100 |
|---|---|---|---:|
| End-market demand | Stable to weak | Global primary aluminium consumption ex-China +1.2% YoY in Q1 2026, China consumption flat; European extrusion demand flat YoY, North American extrusion demand −4% YoY in Q1 2026; full-year 2026 extrusion demand growth estimated at only ~1% [`first-quarter-report-2026.pdf`, p.12, Market statistics table; p.16, Extrusions market development] | 60 |
| Company market share | Not disclosed | Hydro does not publish global market-share figures for aluminium, alumina, or extruded products in this pool; "Not proven from available data" | — |
| Price / realization | Diverging sharply by commodity — aluminium up, alumina down | LME 3-month average price +21.6% YoY (USD 3,192/mt Q1'26 vs USD 2,625/mt Q1'25); realized alumina price −41.2% YoY (USD 345/mt vs USD 587/mt) [`first-quarter-report-2026.pdf`, p.12-13] | 90 |
| Product / customer / geography mix | Improving at the margin | Value-add product premiums (extrusion ingot, recycled billet) rose faster than standard-ingot premiums following the Middle East supply shock, lifting recycling spreads to their strongest level since 2023 [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.5] | 30 |
| FX translation | Deteriorating for reported NOK revenue | USD/NOK average rate fell 12.3% YoY (9.71 in Q1'26 vs 11.07 in Q1'25) — a stronger krone shrinks the NOK value of the same USD-denominated selling price [`first-quarter-report-2026.pdf`, p.13, p.19] | 75 |
| M&A / divestitures | Not a current factor | No revenue-affecting M&A or divestiture is disclosed in this pool for the period under review. The five-segment structure has been stable since FY2022; a "Rolling" business area was divested around FY2020/2021, a historical (not current-period) structural change [`03_segment-map.md`, §3] | — |

This split matters because it shows the FY2026-to-date revenue story is not organic demand growth — it is a commodity-price and currency story overlaid on roughly flat volumes. Do not read the aluminium-price-driven segments' revenue swings as end-market demand growth; global consumption growth is running near +1%, an order of magnitude below the price swings.

## 4. Revenue Driver Table (consolidated)

| Driver | Current Level | Direction | Magnitude | Evidence |

## 6. Revenue Growth Decomposition

**A precise price/volume/mix/FX revenue bridge is not disclosed by the company.** Hydro publishes a detailed Adjusted EBITDA bridge each quarter (price, volume, cost, currency, other effects, in NOK) but does not publish an equivalent bridge at the revenue line — only segment-level realized prices, volumes, and the aggregate revenue figure. Building an exact NOK-for-NOK revenue bridge from these pieces would require assuming a stable quarter-to-quarter segment revenue mix, which the evidence does not support (Bauxite & Alumina's revenue share swings materially with the alumina price cycle — its FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA share alone moved from 41.0% in FY2024 to 32.3% in FY2025 [`03_segment-map.md`, §2]). Forcing pp-level revenue attribution from these inputs would be Inference, not from filings, and is not shown as a fabricated point estimate. Instead, the table below reports what the company itself discloses and attributes, at the quarter it applies to (Q1 2026 vs Q1 2025, the most current comparison, revenue −11.7%).

| Component | Contribution to Growth (pp) | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Alumina price | Not quantified as a revenue-pp by the company; management's own explicit attribution for the quarter's revenue decline | Company language: "revenues fell by around 12%... driven by lower alumina prices" [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6]. Realized alumina price −41% YoY (USD 345/mt vs USD 587/mt) [`first-quarter-report-2026.pdf`, p.9] |
| Aluminium price | Not quantified as a revenue-pp by the company; directionally offsetting (positive) | LME realized price +15% YoY in USD, but only +1% in NOK because of FX (see below) [`first-quarter-report-2026.pdf`, p.13] |
| Volume | Not quantified as a revenue-pp by the company; broadly a small offsetting positive at the primary-metal level, small negative at Extrusions | Alumina production +3.4%, primary aluminium production +2.8%, Aluminium Metal total sales +4.5%, but Extrusion volumes −1.6% and Metal Markets external sales −0.7% [`first-quarter-report-2026.pdf`, p.9, 13, 14, 17] |
| FX (USD/NOK) | Not quantified as a revenue-pp by the company; a materially negative translation effect on USD-linked revenue | USD/NOK average −12.3% YoY (9.71 vs 11.07); the company's disclosed *EBITDA* sensitivity is NOK 4,900m per NOK 1.00 move (~17% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA) — the revenue-level effect of the same FX move is not separately disclosed but is directionally larger given EBITDA margin is well below 100% of revenue [`first-quarter-report-2026.pdf`, p.13, 19; FY2025 Annual Report, p.38] |
| Mix / M&A / Other | Not quantified — no material M&A in the period | Not proven from available data |
| **Total revenue growth** | **−11.7%** (NOK 57,094m → NOK 50,388m) | [`first-quarter-report-2026.pdf`, p.5-6] |

**What's missing:** a company-published revenue-level price/volume/currency bridge (only an EBITDA-level bridge and per-segment realized-price/volume tables exist in this pool). A secondary, annual-basis comparison (FY2025 vs FY2024, revenue +2.1%, NOK 203,636m → NOK 207,971m) shows the same tension in the other direction: realized alumina price fell 6.5% (USD 462/mt → USD 432/mt) while realized aluminium price rose 8.4% (USD 2,374/mt → USD 2,573/mt) and USD/NOK weakened 3.3% (10.75 → 10.39) [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.37, "Key financial data"] — again, without a formal bridge, the exact pp split between these is not derivable from disclosure.

## 7. The Single Biggest Revenue Driver

**The LME aluminium price is the single biggest revenue driver, and its current direction is a geopolitically-driven spike, not a normalized run-rate.** The price runs through nearly every segment's selling price, either directly (Aluminium Metal's realized price is LME-plus-premium) or contractually (alumina is sold on an index linked to the LME with a one-month lag; Metal Markets and Extrusions price their metal-linked products off LME-plus-conversion-margin) [`03_segment-map.md`, row 1; `first-quarter-report-2026.pdf`, p.13]. A 10-20% move in the LME price therefore does not stay contained to the 7.1%-of-revenue Aluminium Metal segment — it flows into the selling prices behind the 36.4%-of-revenue Metal Markets and 37.5%-of-revenue Extrusions lines too, even though those segments add conversion margin on top. The current direction is up sharply: the 3-month LME price moved from USD 2,995/mt to above USD 3,400/mt within Q1 2026 alone (+~16% intra-quarter), a move management attributes directly to the Middle East conflict and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz cutting off roughly 9% of global output and 4-5 million tonnes/year of exports [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.4]. This is explicitly not a demand-driven, repeatable move — it is a supply-shock spike, and the company's own forward booking data shows the market already pricing some reversal: only 67% of Q2 2026 primary production is booked, at USD 3,000/mt, below the USD 3,467/mt level the quarter ended at [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6]. The USD/NOK exchange rate is the second-largest lever and works as a partial offset in the same period (a 12.3% weaker USD/NOK subtracted from the aluminium-price gain, per §6) — but it is a transmission mechanism for the same underlying price, not an independent driver of comparable size on its own disclosed sensitivity (NOK 4,900m of Adjusted EBITDA, a profit measure, per NOK 1.00 move [FY2025 Annual Report, p.38]).

**Cycle-position note (required for a commodity/policy-exposed business):** the latest reported period is not a normalized run-rate on two of its three biggest price inputs. The LME aluminium price (3-month average USD 3,192/mt in Q1 2026, quarter-end USD 3,467/mt) sits well above the FY2023-FY2025 realized-price band of USD 2,218-2,573/mt [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.37] and is explicitly tied to a one-time geopolitical supply shock (Middle East conflict, Strait of Hormuz closure) rather than a structural demand shift — call this a price spike/peak, and label it non-run-rate; it can reverse quickly if the conflict resolves or curtailed Middle East and Chinese capacity returns [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.4-5]. The alumina price (Platts PAX USD 307/mt in Q1 2026) sits below the FY2023-FY2025 realized-price band of USD 359-462/mt [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.37] — a trough, driven by structural oversupply from new Indonesian and Indian refinery capacity plus Middle-East-related demand destruction, not obviously reversible on the same short horizon. Extrusions' end-market demand — construction and industrial — is, in the company's own words, "stabilized at historically low levels" [`first-quarter-report-2026.pdf`, p.16], a cyclical trough consistent with the High industrial-cycle and consumer-cycle dependency the business-model module flags [`10_external-dependency.md`, rows "Industrial cycle" and "Consumer cycle"]. This reconciles with, and reinforces, the business-model module's own "Mostly externally driven" classification (External Dependency Risk Score 74/100, inverted — higher is worse) [`10_external-dependency.md`, §3-4]: none of the three biggest revenue inputs (aluminium price, alumina price, extrusion demand) is currently at a level that can be extrapolated forward without an explicit reversal risk flagged.

# Margin Drivers — NHY

## 1. Segment Decomposition Status

Business-model `03_segment-map.md` is available and used. Norsk Hydro reports five operating segments (Hydro Bauxite & Alumina, Hydro Energy, Hydro Aluminium Metal, Hydro Metal Markets, Hydro Extrusions) plus an immaterial "Other and Eliminations" bucket, with full segment-level revenue, EBIT, EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, D&A, capex and assets disclosed in Note 1.4 of the FY2025 Integrated Annual Report [Integrated Annual Report 2025, Note 1.4, p.149-151]. No segment exceeds 85% of revenue or profit — Hydro Extrusions is the largest revenue segment (37.5% FY2025 external revenue) while Hydro Aluminium Metal is the largest profit segment (39.5% FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA) — so this is a genuine multi-segment decomposition, not a single-segment consolidated read [`business-model/03_segment-map.md`, §1-2]. Drivers are therefore decomposed by segment in §6 below, and the consolidated view (§2-5, §7-8) is built up from, and cross-checked against, the segment detail.

## 3. Gross Margin → EBITDA Margin → EBIT Margin Walk

The table below is retained (Hydro's raw-material-and-energy expense functions economically like a COGS line, so the ladder is meaningful) but is supplementary to Table A above, which is the sector-appropriate primary read.

| Margin Level | FY2025 | FY2024 | Change (bps) | Main Reason | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Gross margin¹ | 35.99% | 36.48% | -49 | Raw material and energy expense grew slightly faster than revenue (64.00% vs 63.53% of revenue) | [Integrated Annual Report 2025, Note 5.3, p.187; `01_historical-financials.md` §1] |
| EBITDA margin (reported) | 12.36% | 13.03% | -67 | FY2025 included a larger negative swing in unrealized derivative timing (adjustment moved from -225 in FY2024 to +3,193 in FY2025, i.e., FY2025 reported EBITDA understates the underlying trend versus FY2024) plus higher restructuring/rationalization costs | [`01_historical-financials.md` §4] |
| EBIT margin (reported) | 6.92% | 8.10% | -118 | Same drivers as EBITDA, plus a larger FY2025 impairment charge (NOK 1,148mn vs NOK 39mn), concentrated in the five-plant Extrusions closure | [Integrated Annual Report 2025, Note 2.5, p.6322; `01_historical-financials.md` §1] |
| Adjusted EBITDA margin (company APM, quarterly) | 17.20% (Q1'26) | 16.67% (Q1'25) | +54 (YoY) | Recovered sharply after a Q4'25 trough (11.83%) on higher realized aluminium prices, stronger downstream/recycling margins, and normalizing eliminations — see §7 bridge | [`01_historical-financials.md` §3] |

¹ CIQ reclassification (revenue less raw material and energy expense), not a company-disclosed subtotal — flagged per `01_historical-financials.md`.

**Pass-through lag.** Hydro does not "pass through" costs to customers in a retail sense — it is a price-taker on both its main input (alumina, for the smelting segments) and its main output (LME aluminium) — but the pricing mechanisms carry stated, evidenced lags: alumina bought or sold externally is "priced with reference to alumina spot price indexes" with a one-month delay [Integrated Annual Report 2025, Note 8.2, p.186-187], and realized aluminium prices "lag the LME price developments by approximately 1.5-2 months," including the effect of Hydro's own LME strategic hedging program [first-quarter-report-2026.pdf, p.7, footnote 4]. This means a sudden LME move (such as the Q1 2026 spike from USD 2,995/mt to above USD 3,400/mt) shows up in realized results with a roughly 1.5-2 month delay, so its full effect is still flowing through into Q2 2026 rather than having been fully captured in the Q1 2026 print.

## 4. Margin Walk — Which Margin Level Matters Most?

**Adjusted EBITDA margin, read at the segment level, is the most useful metric for this business.** Reported EBITDA and EBIT are distorted quarter to quarter by large, non-cash, unrealized derivative mark-to-market swings on LME-linked contracts — the FY2023-FY2025 adjustment to EBITDA flipped sign each year (-1,033 in FY2023, -225 in FY2024, +3,193 in FY2025) and Q4 2025 reported EBITDA collapsed to NOK 1,974mn (a 4.2% margin) almost entirely on one such timing loss before recovering in Q1 2026 [`01_historical-financials.md` §3-4]. Gross margin is a CIQ-only construct with no company subtotal behind it. Adjusted EBITDA margin, and its segment-level Adjusted EBITDA components, is both the metric management itself uses to run the business (it is the profit-share basis in the segment map) and the metric least distorted by hedge-accounting timing — it is the right level to track whether the underlying price-cost spread, not derivative noise, is improving or worsening.

## 7. Margin Bridge — Latest Period

Hydro discloses its own Adjusted EBITDA bridge in NOK million (not in margin basis points) between consecutive quarters — Q4 2025 (NOK 5,587mn) to Q1 2026 (NOK 8,668mn), a change of +NOK 3,100mn (management's own rounded figure; the exact underlying figures are NOK 5,587mn and NOK 8,668mn, an implied +NOK 3,081mn) [`01_historical-financials.md` §3; Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6-7]. The table below reproduces the CFO's own component breakdown verbatim from the earnings call, cited to the primary/verbatim transcript:

| Component (as reported by management) | Margin Impact (NOK million) | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Realized all-in aluminium and alumina prices (net) | +1,200 | [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6] |
| Upstream volumes (Bauxite & Alumina lower, Aluminium Metal slightly higher, net) | -300 | [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6] |
| Raw material costs (higher energy/carbon in Aluminium Metal) | -50 | [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6] |
| Extrusions — seasonal sales-volume increase | +650 | [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6] |
| Extrusions — margin effect | +500 | [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6] |
| Metal Markets — recycling improvement | +100 | [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6] |
| Energy business area (lower production, loss of price-area differences) | -500 | [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6] |
| Fixed cost (NOK 300mn lower in Extrusions, NOK 200mn lower in Bauxite & Alumina) | +550 | [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6] |
| FX (stronger NOK vs. USD) | -700 | [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6] |
| Other (commercial activities in Metal Markets/Bauxite & Alumina, plus NOK 600mn release of previously eliminated internal margins) | +1,600 | [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6] |
| **Total (sum of components)** | **≈ +3,050** | Reconciles to management's own rounded "+NOK 3.1 billion" within normal rounding of verbal component figures |

This is a NOK-value EBITDA bridge, not a margin-percentage bridge — Hydro does not disclose a component-level bps breakdown. The aggregate margin move it corresponds to is verified separately: Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 11.83% (Q4'25) to 17.20% (Q1'26), +537bps [`01_historical-financials.md` §3]. Attempting to convert each NOK component above into a standalone bps figure would require allocating a revenue base across components that Hydro does not disclose, and is not attempted here — doing so would be inference presented as precision.

## 8. The Single Biggest Margin Driver

**The LME aluminium price — specifically, how much of its current level is a one-time supply-shock premium rather than a durable price.** Hydro Aluminium Metal is the largest single contributor to group Adjusted EBITDA (39.5% of FY2025, and roughly 6.7x Bauxite & Alumina's contribution in Q1 2026), and the company's own disclosed sensitivity is +NOK 150mn of Adjusted EBITDA per +USD 10/mt of aluminium price [`business-model/03_segment-map.md`, §2; `business-model/10_external-dependency.md`, §2]. The Q1 2026 price move — from USD 2,995/mt to above USD 3,400/mt within the quarter — was driven explicitly by a Middle East conflict, regional production curtailments (~40% of Qatalum), and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a region that supplies "some 9%" of global aluminium output and exports 4-5 million tonnes a year [Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.4]. This is a textbook one-time, non-run-rate supply shock, not demand-led growth. If the shock unwinds — Gulf capacity resumes, the strait reopens, or China curtails more supply to rebalance the market as management itself flags as the open question for 2027 — a reversion of even USD 400/mt (back toward the pre-shock USD 2,995/mt-2,300/mt range) implies roughly NOK 6.0bn of Adjusted EBITDA downside on the disclosed sensitivity, about 21% of FY2025 group Adjusted EBITDA of NOK 28,889mn. The current level of realized aluminium price is therefore the single variable most likely, if it reverses, to compress group margins the most — and it is currently a tailwind resting on a geopolitical shock rather than a structural improvement.

| FQ1 2026 (Mar-2026) | Beat | Beat | Rev +0.3% / EPS +34.4% | Actual revenue NOK 50,388m vs consensus NOK 50,242.7m [`first-quarter-report-2026.pdf`, Condensed consolidated statements of income]; actual Adjusted EPS NOK 2.07 vs consensus NOK 1.54 [`first-quarter-report-2026.pdf`, Key figures — "Adjusted earnings per share... 2.07"]. See the Section 1 reconciliation flag: the recomputed +34.4% EPS / +0.3% revenue surprise differs from the transcript cover page's own stated +24.70% / +1.46% |

[Source for FQ2–FQ4 2025: `NorskHydroASAOBNHYEstimatesReport.xls`, Surprise tab, Fiscal Quarters section; cross-checked against the FQ1 2026 and FQ4 2025 transcript cover pages]

Revenue has beaten Street consensus in all four of the last four quarters, though by shrinking, then re-widening, margins (+3.3%, +6.0%, +1.5%, +0.3%). EPS is more mixed — two beats bracketing two misses, with the most recent quarter's beat unusually large. There is no clean pattern of the company consistently sandbagging or consistently missing; the last print (FQ1 2026) was the strongest EPS beat of the four.

## 7. Bar Assessment

**Bar is low.**

FY2026 EPS Normalized, EBITDA, and revenue consensus were all cut in the 30 days immediately before this report's as-of date (2026-07-15), and the cut is broadest and clearest at exactly the metric and quarter that matters most right now: zero analysts raised FQ2 2026 EPS in the last month while four cut it, and FQ2 2026 EBITDA fell ~9.5% in the same window — this is the module's own low-bar trigger ("estimates have been cut recently"), landing just three days before the 22-Jul-2026 print. The cuts track the company's own Q2 bridge commentary (higher energy/carbon/raw-material costs, lower Aluminium Metal volumes from the Middle East situation) rather than looking like an independent, unexplained Street markdown — but FQ2 2026 revenue itself was still revised net-upward in the same window (3 up, 1 down), so the reset is margin-specific, not a broad-based demand cut, which argues the bar has been lowered on costs the Street may be over-extrapolating rather than on volumes. The one guidance-comparable metric available (FY2026 capex) shows the Street modeling ~6.5% more spend than management guided, which — if capex undershoots toward the company's own NOK 13,500m plan — is a second, independent way the setup could beat on free cash flow even without an EBITDA beat. This bar read is not provisional under the stale-consensus guard: the consensus data-as-of date (2026-07-15) sits after the last reported quarter (FQ1 2026, 29-Apr-2026) and only three days before the next print, so it is current, not stale.

# Beat / Miss Setup — NHY

## 1. Next Quarter Context

The next print is FQ2 2026 (quarter ended 30-Jun-2026), releasing **22-Jul-2026 — three days after this report's as-of date** [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §1; Consensus/Trends tab headers]. No formal seasonality read exists for Norsk Hydro from this data pool (`01_historical-financials.md` §5 — insufficient quarterly history), so this is not a seasonally-flagged quarter in either direction, though Extrusions volumes typically step up from Q1 to Q2 (§6 below). Street consensus going into the print, as of 15-Jul-2026, is Revenue NOK 55,954.2m, EBITDA NOK 8,581.8m, EPS Normalized (Adjusted EPS) NOK 2.01 [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §4] — and `04_guidance-consensus.md` explicitly assesses this bar as **"low"** (§7), because FY2026 and FQ2 2026 EPS/EBITDA estimates were cut sharply (FQ2 EBITDA −9.5%, zero analysts raised FQ2 EPS) in the 30 days right before the print, tracking the company's own guided Q2 cost bridge, while FQ2 revenue estimates were still net-raised over the same window.

## 2. Beat Scenarios

| Capex undershoots the Street's higher model, lifting free cash flow | Capex guidance vs consensus (`04_guidance-consensus.md` §3) | Actual FQ2/FY2026 capex tracks management's guided NOK 13,500m total rather than the Street's NOK 14,377.4m (~6.5% higher) model | Mid-High | [Guidance tab, dated 2026-02-13; `04_guidance-consensus.md` §3] |

Threshold is inference from the historical surprise range, not company-set. *Inference, not from filings.* |

A large reported miss or beat may say more about hedge-accounting timing than the underlying business — cross-check against Adjusted EBITDA before treating a reported-EBITDA surprise as real. *Inference, not from filings.* |
| EPS | NOK 2.01 Normalized/Adjusted (FQ2 2026, Street) | > +20% (above the largest prior "clean" beat magnitude context) | > −10% (in line with the two prior misses, −6.8% and −12.8%) | EPS surprises over the last 4 quarters ranged from −12.8% to +34.4% [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §6] — a wide, unstable band, so a modest single-digit surprise in either direction sits within normal noise; only outsized moves are informative. *Inference, not from filings.* |
| Guidance | No formal group guidance issued (capex only: NOK 13,500m FY2026) | Capex tracking near or below NOK 13,500m guided (vs Street's NOK 14,377.4m) | Capex re-guided materially above NOK 13,500m, or a new formal outlook signals group-level deterioration | Capex is the only line with a clean guidance-vs-consensus gap; the Street already models more spend than guided [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §3] |

## 5. In-Line Print But Bad Guidance Risk

| Risk | Evidence | Why It Matters |

| In-line current quarter but the Q2 cost bridge already flags a further, unquantified alumina-price headwind into Q3 | The company's own Q2 segment bridge names "lower alumina price (negative, unquantified)" for Bauxite & Alumina and cites a structural 2.7-3.0 million tonne 2026 global oversupply — a trough that is "not obviously reversible on the same short horizon" [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §2; `02_revenue-drivers.md` §7] | Even a clean FQ2 print does not resolve the structural alumina overhang that could keep pressuring one of the five segments into H2 2026 |
| Beat on EBITDA/EPS but working capital deteriorates | Q1 2026 net cash from operating activities was negative NOK (1,891)m against a positive Adjusted EBITDA of NOK 8,668m — an "operating capital build from higher prices and sales" [`06_earnings-quality.md` §2] | A profit beat driven by higher realized prices can be accompanied by a cash-conversion breakdown in the same period if working capital absorbs the gain — worth checking the FQ2 cash-flow statement, not just the P&L headline |
| Beat driven by trading/sourcing gains management itself calls one-off | The NOK 900m Metal Markets "other effects" benefit is explicitly flagged by management as "normalizing" (reverting) into Q2 2026 [`03_margin-drivers.md` §6] | A Q2 beat that leans on this line repeating would be a quality-flag, not a durable improvement — management has already told the market to expect it to fade |
| Beat on revenue via the still-elevated LME price, but that price is explicitly a one-time supply-shock premium | LME price move from USD 2,995/mt to above USD 3,400/mt attributed directly to the Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz closure — flagged as "NOT run-rate" [`03_margin-drivers.md` §8] | A revenue/EBITDA beat riding this price does not by itself signal an improved underlying business; the same driver is the largest single reversal risk (§3) |

## 6. Seasonality Read

`01_historical-financials.md` §5 states plainly that a formal seasonality table cannot be built for Hydro from this pool — only FY2023-FY2025 annual figures and 5 individual quarters (several approximate) exist, spanning a period of falling alumina and aluminium prices rather than a repeatable calendar pattern. The one seasonality-adjacent data point available is Extrusions volume, which rose 15.7% quarter-on-quarter from Q4 2025 to Q1 2026 and is described in that context as "seasonal" [`02_revenue-drivers.md` §5], and the company's own Q2 2026 bridge for Extrusions explicitly guides "higher sales volumes" versus Q2 2025 [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §2]. This is a mild, single-segment tailwind for the setup — not a group-level seasonality effect — and should not be read as evidence the whole print is seasonally favored.

## 7. Historical Pattern

`04_guidance-consensus.md` §6 shows revenue beating Street consensus in all four of the last four quarters (magnitudes +3.3%, +6.0%, +1.5%, +0.3% — shrinking, then re-widening slightly), which is a real, repeatable signal worth moderate weight for the revenue line specifically. EPS is a different story: two beats bracket two misses (+15.1%, −12.8%, −6.8%, +34.4%), with no clean sandbagging or overshooting pattern — the swings are large in both directions and, per `01_historical-financials.md` §4 and `06_earnings-quality.md` §4, are heavily influenced by non-cash, sign-flipping derivative timing adjustments rather than a consistent operating trend. The synthesizer should weight the revenue beat streak as a moderate positive signal, but should not extend that confidence to EPS — the historical pattern there is closer to a coin flip with wide variance, not a directional edge.

## 8. Setup Verdict

**Setup favors beat.**

The single most important factor is that FQ2 2026 EBITDA/EPS consensus was cut sharply (FQ2 EBITDA −9.5%, zero analysts raised FQ2 EPS) in the last 30 days specifically to match management's own guided Q2 cost bridge (energy, carbon, B&A fixed-cost seasonality) — a mechanical de-risking of the bar just before the print — while FQ2 revenue estimates stayed net-positive over the same window and the company's own booking data shows a third of Q2 aluminium production still unbooked at a spot price (USD 3,467/mt at Q1 quarter-end) well above the USD 3,000/mt already locked in for the booked two-thirds [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §4-5, §7; Q1 2026 transcript, prepared remarks, p.6]. The single biggest risk that could flip this verdict is the Metal Markets trading-gain reversal (§3) landing harder than management's own "normalizing" guidance implies, or the guided cost ranges (energy/carbon/fixed cost) landing above their top ends — either would erase the low-bar advantage on the metric (EBITDA/EPS) where the bar has moved lowest, even if revenue beats again.

## 9. Second-Quarter Look-Ahead

FQ3 2026 has materially less visibility: management's own quantified bridge covers only one quarter forward (Q2 2026 vs Q1 2026), so no comparable cost/price bridge exists for Q3 in this pool [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §2]. Two structural factors point toward a tougher setup by Q3 than Q2: the alumina oversupply is described as a multi-quarter, not obviously reversible trough (§5), and Extrusions demand recovery is explicitly pushed to "H2" with only ~1% full-year 2026 growth guided for both Europe and North America [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §2]. The LME price reversal risk (§3) also becomes more relevant by Q3, since a smaller share of Q3 production would likely be pre-booked at the current elevated hedge rate than Q2's already-locked two-thirds. Not proven from available data whether these effects net to a harder or easier Q3 bar — only that the visibility is lower and the known headwinds (alumina, extrusion demand) skew toward persistence rather than resolution within one quarter.

## 10. Pre-Mortem

If this "favors beat" setup fails, the most likely reason is that the Street's late estimate cuts did not fully capture the guided cost ranges — energy, carbon, and B&A seasonal fixed costs landed above their top-end guided figures, or the flagged Metal Markets trading-gain reversal was steeper than "normalizing" implied — eroding the low-bar advantage on EBITDA/EPS even as revenue kept its 4-quarter beat streak alive. A second plausible failure mode is that the Middle East supply shock unwound faster than the company's own booking data assumed, pulling the unbooked ~33% of Q2 aluminium volume down toward pre-shock spot levels before it could be sold at the elevated price this setup is counting on.

# Earnings Quality — NHY

Norsk Hydro ASA reports under IFRS Accounting Standards as adopted by the EU, in Norwegian Krone (NOK million), fiscal year ending 31 December [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.140]. Figures below are company-reported (audited) or company-disclosed Alternative Performance Measures (APMs) unless labelled as a Capital IQ (CIQ) vendor field; per the data-quality note in `01_historical-financials.md`, CIQ's own EBITDA/EBIT reclassification for Hydro does not reconcile to the audited figures and is not used here — company-reported EBITDA/EBIT (audited "Other performance measures" table) are used instead [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.36].

Cash flow data is available (full Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows for FY2021–FY2025, plus Q1 2026) — the partial-data cap for missing cash flow data does not apply.

## 1. EBITDA → CFO → FCF Bridge (5 years)

Currency: NOK million. Basis: company-reported (audited) EBITDA for FY2023–FY2025; company-reported EBITDA/EBIT are **not disclosed for FY2021–FY2022 in this data pool** (the pre-FY2023 annual report is not in the pool) — these two years are marked N/A rather than estimated [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.36, "Other performance measures" table, FY2023–FY2025 columns only].

[Norsk Hydro ASA OB NHY Financials.xls, Cash Flow tab (CFO, capex, WC change, tax paid, interest paid); Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.36 (EBITDA)]

¹ "Working capital change" is the CIQ Cash Flow tab's own "Change in Net Working Capital" supplemental line (sum of changes in receivables, inventories, payables, and other net operating assets), sign convention: positive = cash inflow [Norsk Hydro ASA OB NHY Financials.xls, Cash Flow tab, "Change in Net Working Capital" row].

² "Other operating items" is a derived plug (CFO minus EBITDA minus the three lines above), not itself a single audited line. It reconciles the audited EBITDA APM (which excludes depreciation & amortization, and nets certain non-operating items differently) to the cash-flow statement, which is built starting from Net Income. It captures the D&A add-back, non-cash unrealized derivative mark-to-market swings on LME/power/raw-material contracts (a structural feature of Hydro's hedge accounting — see §4), income/loss from equity-accounted investees, discontinued operations, and non-cash asset write-downs. Its size and sign volatility (+9,124 / −4,516 / +7,515 across FY2023–FY2025) is itself a quality signal, not a rounding residual — see §2 and §10. FY2021–FY2022 marked N/A because company-reported EBITDA is unavailable for those years (see table header).

³ **Capex split not disclosed — total capex used. FCF may understate true recurring free cash flow.** Norsk Hydro discloses total Capex as an APM (Purchases of PP&E plus other long-term investments, less investment grants received: NOK 12,097m FY2025, NOK 15,078m FY2024) but does not split maintenance/sustaining spend from growth spend in this data pool [Integrated Annual Report 2025, "Capital expenditure (Capex)" APM table, p.233–234]. Management has referred qualitatively to "historically high sustaining capital expenditure" without giving a number [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.51 narrative]. This report's FCF uses the cash-flow-statement capex line (Purchases of PP&E only: NOK 11,582m FY2025) per the module-standard FCF definition (CFO − total capex), which is a narrower capex figure than the company's own broader Capex APM.

**Lead figure — normalised operating FCF vs company FCF APM (§15):** The module-standard FCF above (CFO − total capex) is the **lead figure** in this report. Norsk Hydro also discloses its own **company-defined Free Cash Flow APM**, which nets out changes in derivative collateral and short-term-investment purchases/sales — a different, non-standard definition, not a one-off inflator: **NOK 13,034m FY2025**, **NOK 2,844m FY2024**, and **NOK (3,985m) — negative — for Q1 2026** [Integrated Annual Report 2025, "Free cash flow" APM table, p.233; First Quarter Report 2026, p.37]. The two bases diverge because the company version excludes collateral and short-term-investment cash effects that the module-standard CFO − capex definition does not adjust for. Both are shown, labelled, so they are not conflated: module-standard FY2025 FCF = NOK 11,729m vs company APM NOK 13,034m (a modest NOK 1,305m gap); module-standard FY2024 FCF = NOK 1,801m vs company APM NOK 2,844m (a NOK 1,043m gap). Neither year shows evidence of FCF being inflated by an itemised one-off cash item (e.g., a customer advance) — the gap is a definitional/collateral-netting difference, disclosed and reconciled by the company itself.

## 2. Cash Conversion Assessment

Multi-year cash conversion is decent on average but volatile year to year: CFO/EBITDA was 95.4% in FY2023, fell to 57.9% in FY2024 (below the 70% "healthy" threshold), then recovered to 90.7% in FY2025 — a 3-year average of 81.3%, and the trailing-twelve-month (TTM, ended 31-Mar-2026) figure is 79.4% (TTM CFO NOK 17,440m ÷ TTM EBITDA NOK 21,976m) [derived from `01_historical-financials.md`, §2]. The FY2024 dip tracks a working-capital build (receivables +24.5% YoY and inventory +10.8% YoY, both outpacing revenue/COGS growth — see §6) that partly reversed in FY2025. The most recent standalone quarter is the weak point: Q1 2026 net cash from operating activities was **negative NOK (1,891)m** against a positive Adjusted EBITDA of NOK 8,668m, driven by "operating capital build from higher prices and sales" [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.4 highlights; First Quarter Report 2026, p.37, "Free cash flow" table] — a genuine, disclosed cash-conversion breakdown in the latest quarter, attributable to the ordinary working-capital cycle of a commodity producer riding higher prices, not to accrual manipulation, but a real near-term signal that reported/adjusted profit is currently running ahead of cash.

## 3. Working Capital Trends

Basis: average of opening and closing balances `(FY{-1} closing + FY{0} closing) / 2`. DSO uses revenue as the denominator; DIO and DPO use COGS (Raw material and energy expense), per module formula. [Norsk Hydro ASA OB NHY Financials.xls, Balance Sheet tab (Accounts Receivable, Inventory, Accounts Payable) and Income Statement tab (Revenue, Cost of Goods Sold)]

| Inventory days (DIO) | 82.0 | 75.7 | 76.8 | Fell then flat (−7.7% FY24, +1.4% FY25 YoY) | Low — no build; well under 15% YoY flag threshold |
| Payable days (DPO) | 55.4 | 54.1 | 53.2 | Falling slightly (−2.2% FY24, −1.8% FY25 YoY) | Low-Medium — paying suppliers modestly faster, not stretching them; not a liquidity-stress pattern given the company's net-cash-generative, sub-1x-leverage position (see `01`, §1 footnote 5) |
| Cash conversion cycle (DSO + DIO − DPO) | 58.7 | 54.5 | 56.6 | Stable (54.5–58.7 day range) | Low |

None of the three flag thresholds (DSO rising >10% YoY; DIO rising >15% YoY; DPO rising sharply) are triggered in FY2024 or FY2025. The FY2024 receivables (+24.5% YoY, 16,382→20,396) and inventory (+10.8% YoY, 25,449→28,187) *balance* growth outpaced revenue/COGS growth that year (see §6, accrual quality flags) even though the resulting *days* metrics stayed within threshold — both reversed in FY2025.

**Exceeding 15% of GAAP earnings:** at the EBITDA level the FY2025 adjustment (+3,193 / +12.4% of reported EBITDA) stays under 15%, but at EBIT and net-income level it does not: FY2025 EBIT adjustment +4,262 = **29.6%** of reported EBIT; FY2025 net-income adjustment +2,851 = **34.3%** of reported net income. FY2024 and FY2023 are larger still at the net-income line (see §7). Flagged as a standing concern, not a one-off.

## 9. Earnings Quality Score

**Score: 55/100 — Mixed / average (41–60 band): material concerns from recurring "one-off" charges.**

The single most important reason for this score is that Hydro books "significant rationalization and closure costs" as an EBITDA/EBIT add-back **every single year**, with the amount growing (265 → 407 → 1,795 NOK m over FY2023–FY2025), alongside an impairment charge in every year [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.36–37] — the module rule treats a charge that recurs every period as not genuinely one-off, and the band description (41–60: "material concerns…recurring one-offs") applies directly. This is compounded by a large, persistent gap between reported and adjusted net income/EPS (+34% to +180% across the three years, §7) driven by non-cash derivative and FX swings, which makes reported bottom-line EPS an unreliable stand-alone read of underlying earnings power in any single year. Offsetting factors that keep the score in the middle band rather than lower: cash conversion is decent on a multi-year average (81.3% 3-year avg CFO/EBITDA, 79.4% TTM — both above the 70% "healthy" threshold), working-capital days show no sustained build (§3), receivable factoring is disclosed with a hard cap and was not fully utilized, share-based compensation is immaterial, and every adjustment is transparently reconciled in the audited annual report rather than hidden or vaguely described.

## 10. The Single Biggest Quality Concern

The single biggest risk that reported earnings misstate the economic picture is not fraud or hidden cash weakness — it is that Hydro's reported net income and EPS are dominated, in every one of the last three years, by large non-cash items that sit below the EBITDA line: unrealized derivative mark-to-market timing on LME-linked hedges, impairments, and "significant" rationalization costs that recur annually despite being labelled one-off. Together these pushed reported net income *below* the company's own adjusted net income by 34% (FY2025), 84% (FY2024), and 180% (FY2023) [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.36]. A reader who takes the headline reported EPS (NOK 1.77 in FY2023, for example) at face value without cross-checking the adjusted figure (NOK 4.26) or the cash-flow statement would badly misjudge the year's underlying earnings power. The company discloses this fully and audits it, so it is a volatility-and-interpretation risk rather than a concealment risk — but it means reported net income/EPS should never be used on a standalone basis for this company, and the recurring rationalization add-back (§8) means even the *adjusted* EBITDA figure likely overstates the ongoing cash cost of running Hydro's aging, high-capex asset base by a modest but persistent amount each year.

# Earnings Sensitivity — NHY

## 1. Variable Selection

The six variables below were selected from the "High" and "Mid" magnitude rows of the revenue driver table [`02_revenue-drivers.md`, §4] and margin driver table [`03_margin-drivers.md`, §5], cross-checked against the business-model module's external-dependency table, which independently flags Commodity prices and FX as "High" dependency and Industrial cycle as "High" [`business-model/10_external-dependency.md`, §1]. The two largest are the LME aluminium price and the USD/NOK exchange rate — both "High" magnitude in the driver tables and both carrying a company-disclosed NOK-per-unit sensitivity, which makes them the highest-confidence entries here. Alumina price is included because it is the third "High"-magnitude price driver and currently sits below its 3-year band (a trough, per the cycle-position note in `02_revenue-drivers.md` §7). Extrusions external sales volume is included because Extrusions is the largest revenue segment (37.5% of FY2025 external revenue) and its margin has already swung from roughly +4% (2020–2023) to −2.2% (FY2025) [`03_margin-drivers.md`, §6]. Energy & carbon input costs is included despite a "Mid" magnitude rating because it is the only cost driver with company-issued forward quarterly guidance (a rare high-confidence read on a cost line). Recycling spread / Middle East premium normalization is included because both upstream reports repeatedly flag it as a real but explicitly "not fully run-rate" tailwind that management itself has guided will fade ("normalizing") into Q2 2026.
