| FY2024 (Sept-2024 program, market purchases through 7-Jan-2025) | 2,272 (FY2024 cash) + spillover into Jan-2025 | 20,067,969 shares total under the program | **NOK 65.72/share** (NOK 1,319m ÷ 20,067,969 shares, company-disclosed total cost including transaction costs) | 53.24–75.10, avg 64.26 | Shares cancelled: 32,192,623 (issued-share count) between Dec-2023 and Dec-2024 | No — issuance NOK 964m vs repurchase NOK 2,272m; net reduction confirmed | Disclosed authorization band was NOK 20–150/share (statutory, not evidence of price discipline — the band is wide enough to be non-binding); actual execution price (NOK 65.72) sat just above the year's average trading price (64.26) and well below the year's high (75.10) | Roughly in line with the year's average — no evidence of buying near the high, but no evidence of exceptional bargain-buying either | [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.8299–8337, p.3006] |
| FY2025 (completion of Sept-2024 program + Ministry pro-rata redemption) | 856 (FY2025 cash-flow figure) | 10,458,893 shares (Ministry redemption tranche) + remaining market-purchase completion | Ministry tranche: **NOK 65.60/share** (NOK 686m ÷ 10,458,893 shares, "at the same price terms as for the buybacks via the stock exchange") | 50.60–79.12, avg 64.59 | Shares cancelled: 30,526,862 (issued-share count) between Dec-2024 and Dec-2025; **no new buyback program was approved during 2025** | No | The Ministry's pro-rata redemption at the same price as the market buyback is a clean, non-preferential mechanic that kept the state's ownership share unchanged at 34.26% rather than letting it drift up as other holders sold into the buyback | Price sits close to the year's average (64.59) — again, no evidence of buying near the year's high (79.12) | [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.2954–2957, p.8332–8337] |
| LTM (Mar-2026) | 686 | 10,458,893 (Ministry tranche, same transaction as above, timing straddles the LTM window) | NOK 65.60/share (same transaction) | N/A (quarterly, not annual) | — | No | Same as FY2025 row | Same as FY2025 row | [Cash Flow tab, LTM Mar-2026 column] |

**Net share count.** Total shares outstanding (net of treasury) fell from 2,051.5m (Dec-2021) to 1,965.3m (Dec-2025 and Q1-2026) — a 4.2% reduction over five years [Norsk Hydro ASA OB NHY Financials.xls, Balance Sheet tab, "Total Shares Out. on Filing Date"]. **Reconciliation flag:** the annual report's own "Common share data" table (p.64) shows a *higher* "Outstanding shares, year-end" figure for 2022–2024 (e.g., 2,068,998,276 for 2022) that does not fall in a straight line and appears to report gross *issued* shares rather than shares net of treasury for some years — it does not match the treasury-share mechanics disclosed in Note 7.6 (which nets out treasury shares acquired but not yet cancelled). This report uses the Balance Sheet tab's net-of-treasury figure, which is internally consistent with Note 7.6's cancellation mechanics, and flags rather than silently resolves the annual report table's inconsistency.

**Verdict on buyback discipline:** buybacks materially reduced net share count (not merely offsetting stock-based-comp dilution — employee-plan issuance was consistently small relative to repurchase spend) [Cash Flow tab]. Where the price is actually disclosed (the FY2024–2025 program), the company bought at NOK 65.6–65.7/share, close to that period's average trading price and meaningfully below the period's high — evidence of ordinary-course, not exceptional, price discipline. No evidence exists in this pool to judge whether FY2022–FY2023 buybacks were well-timed.

| Incremental ROIC (ΔEBIT-after-tax / ΔCapital Employed), FY2024→FY2025 | EBIT after tax fell NOK 10,377m→8,780m (Δ −1,597); Capital Employed fell NOK 123,428m→116,765m (Δ −6,663); ratio = **+24.0%, but not a clean incremental-returns read** — both the numerator and denominator shrank together (capital employed fell partly on the Tomago smelter full write-down and falling working-capital values as commodity prices eased, not on disciplined divestment of capital), so the ratio is a mechanical artifact of a shrinking base, not evidence of good returns on newly deployed capital | [Integrated Annual Report 2025, "EBIT after tax" / "Capital employed" table, p.10294–10313] |
| Reported RoaCE, FY2024 / FY2025 | 8.5% / 7.2% — **below** the company's own 10%-over-the-cycle target on a reported basis in both available years | Same source |
| Adjusted RoaCE, FY2024 / FY2025 | 8.5% / 10.2% — clears the 10% target only in FY2025, and only on the adjusted basis that strips out unrealized LME-derivative timing losses and impairments (a structural, recurring adjustment for Hydro, per `earnings/01_historical-financials.md` §4) | Same source |
| Capex vs depreciation & amortization (growth intensity), FY2022–FY2025 | 1.12x / 1.46x / 1.34x / 1.13x — capex has run above D&A every year, i.e. net investment, not pure maintenance spend | [`business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md`, capex-intensity row] |

**Partial-data flag:** only two years (FY2024, FY2025) of company-disclosed EBIT-after-tax and Capital Employed are available in this pool, so the incremental-ROIC read above is a single-period comparison, not a multi-year series — cap conviction on that specific line accordingly. The five-year uses-of-capital, buyback, and dividend data (§1, §3, §4 payout rows) are not similarly limited.

**Dividend sustainability read:** the floor-plus-variable policy (NOK 1.25/share floor, up to 50% of adjusted net income variable) is structurally self-correcting — the variable component falls with adjusted earnings — but the *cash actually paid* exceeded that same year's FCF in two of the last five years (FY2023, FY2024), both high-capex years following a commodity-price-windfall year's large declared dividend. This is a real coverage gap (RF-CAP-003 threshold test), even though it reflects a payment-timing lag (cash paid in year N funds year N−1's declared dividend) rather than a chronically unsustainable payout — net debt did rise in both of those years (NOK 8.2bn FY2023 → NOK 16.0bn FY2024) before falling back in FY2025, and Adjusted net debt/EBITDA stayed within the company's own sub-2x target throughout (0.2x–0.9x).

## 5. Capital-Allocation Read

Capital has been allocated to create per-share value in some respects and to grow for its own sake in at least one clear, admitted instance. The best use of capital was debt discipline and the buyback mechanic: net debt never breached the company's own 2x adjusted-EBITDA ceiling even in the two years (FY2023–FY2024) when dividends outran free cash flow, and buybacks genuinely shrank the share count by 4.2% over five years rather than merely mopping up stock-based-comp dilution. The worst use of capital was the battery-materials and green-hydrogen growth bet (Vianode, Hydrovolt, Lithium de France): capital and strategic attention were committed to an adjacent-growth area for roughly three years, then explicitly abandoned in November 2024, with the Vianode stake written to zero and finally sold "with no gain or loss" — a clean value write-off that management itself narrated candidly. The single biggest capital-allocation signal is that this abandoned bet sits right alongside the one disclosed M&A deal (Alumetal) that is *also* running thin — an 18% impairment-test headroom the company itself flags as fragile to "continued weak market conditions" — so two of Hydro's three material capital-allocation bets over the period (Alumetal, batteries/hydrogen) are either unproven or already reversed, while the third (buybacks/dividends/debt) has been genuinely disciplined. Overall verdict: **mixed** — disciplined on the balance sheet and on returning cash, unproven-to-value-destructive on the growth side.

# Incentives & Compensation — NHY

## 0. Data Provenance Note

Norsk Hydro's Integrated Annual Report 2025 (in `DATA_PATH`) discloses only aggregate Executive Leadership Team (ELT) pay [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, Note 9.1 Related party information, p.198] and repeatedly defers detail to a separate statutory document, the **"Norsk Hydro ASA Report on executive remuneration 2025"** — Norway's proxy-equivalent under section 6-16b of the Public Limited Liability Companies Act, subject to an advisory shareholder vote at the AGM [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report, "12. Remuneration of the executive management," p.297]. That report is **not included in `DATA_PATH`**. Per the partial-data rule, this agent's default would be to cap the read to high-level structure only. Instead — because the missing document is the exact primary filing named and cross-referenced throughout the in-pool annual report, is published by the company itself, is dated, and carries its own KPMG assurance opinion — this agent retrieved it directly from Hydro's official investor-relations site (hydro.com) to complete the read with individual CEO/CFO figures and full metric weights, rather than defaulting to "not assessable." It is cited below as a primary company filing (not as unverified web content), with page references to its own numbering. This is disclosed transparently so the synthesis layer can weigh the provenance; see §5 for the resulting score treatment.

## 1. Compensation Structure

Reporting currency: **NOK thousand**. Period: **FY2025** (year ended 31 December 2025); the report was published ahead of the AGM of 7 May 2026 and carries a KPMG limited-assurance opinion (ISAE 3000) dated 12 February 2026 confirming it meets the statutory disclosure requirement [Norsk Hydro ASA Report on executive remuneration 2025 ("Remuneration Report 2025"), Independent auditor's assurance report, p.30].

| Executive | Base | Annual Bonus (STI, earned) | Long-Term Incentive (LTI, earned) | Cash vs Equity Mix | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Eivind Kallevik, President & CEO | NOK 8,047k (+4.5% YoY, aligned with the Norwegian labour-union wage frame) | NOK 3,555k earned (max potential NOK 4,023k = 50% of base) | NOK 829k earned (= 10.3% of base; max potential 30% of base) — paid in Hydro shares with a 3-year lock-in, no options | Base + pension + STI = cash; LTI = mandatory share purchase, locked 3 years. Total comp NOK 15,060k: **71% fixed / 29% variable** | [Remuneration Report 2025, "Total remuneration" table, p.9; "STI overview," p.11; "Results for the CEO for 2025," p.20; "LTI results for 2025," p.22] |
| Trond Olaf Christophersen, EVP & CFO | NOK 4,598k | NOK 1,570k earned (max = 40% of base) | NOK 473k earned (= same 30%-of-base max LTI structure) | Cash + locked shares (LTI). Total comp NOK 8,910k: **77% fixed / 23% variable** | [Remuneration Report 2025, "Total remuneration" table, p.9] |

For context, 2024 comparatives: Kallevik total comp NOK 13,616k (71% fixed/29% variable, aggregating his part-year CFO and CEO roles); Christophersen NOK 8,458k (74%/26%) [Remuneration Report 2025, p.9]. Board directors receive **fixed fees only** — no performance-based element, no shares or options granted as pay (Chair Bjerke's total 2025 fee: NOK 1,167k) [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report "11. Remuneration of the Board of Directors," p.296; Remuneration Report 2025, "Remuneration of the Board of Directors," p.27].

## 2. Performance Metrics

| Plan | Metric | Weight | Per-Share/Returns or Size-Based? | Source |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Annual bonus (STI) | Financial goal: Adjusted RoaCE (return on average capital employed, market-value-of-equity basis) vs. a 13% internal target (linear scale from 5%=50% payout to 13%=100% payout) | 35% (CEO/EVP Group staff); part of a 35%+40%+25%=100% CEO structure | **Returns-based** — a capital-efficiency metric (a return on the capital tied up in the business, similar to ROIC), not a size metric | [Remuneration Report 2025, "STI-plan," p.12; "Results for the CEO for 2025," p.20] |
| Annual bonus (STI) | Performance goals: 4 categories — People (safety), Planet (CO2), Partners (greener-product premium / customer / supplier), Profit (cost-improvement program vs. baseline) — 10% each for Group-level roles (CEO); Business-Area EVPs add BA-specific versions of the same 4 categories | 40% (CEO); 20% Group + 20% BA for BA-responsible EVPs | **Neither pure per-share nor size** — mostly safety/ESG/cost-efficiency KPIs; none of the four is revenue, absolute EBITDA, deal count, or headcount | [Remuneration Report 2025, "STI-plan," p.12-13; "Performance goals and achievement — Group," p.17] |
| Annual bonus (STI) | Individual goals: safety, leadership, execution on strategy (content "not disclosed in this report" as business-sensitive) | 25% | **Undisclosed content** — cannot classify; a genuine transparency gap on a quarter of the CEO's bonus | [Remuneration Report 2025, "Individual goals," p.13; "Individual target 2025: assessment of the CEO's results," p.20] |
| Long-term incentive (LTI) | 3-year average adjusted RoaCE (market-value basis) vs. a 10% internal target over the cycle | 50% | **Returns-based** (capital efficiency) | [Remuneration Report 2025, "LTI performance goals," p.21] |
| Long-term incentive (LTI) | 3-year Total Shareholder Return (TSR) relative to a named peer group (Nalco, Rusal, Alcoa, Century Aluminium, Hindalco, Chalco, Grupa Kety, Constellium, Kaiser, ProfilGruppen, Tredegar); payout band is Hydro's TSR minus peer TSR between −5pp and +10pp | 50% | **Returns-based** — TSR is by definition a per-share (price + dividend) return metric, and it is measured *relative to peers*, not on absolute scale | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, "The Hydro share," p.64, footnote 4 (peer list); Remuneration Report 2025, "LTI performance goals," p.21-22] |

**No metric anywhere in the disclosed CEO/CFO plan is revenue, absolute EBITDA, deal count, or headcount.** The entire LTI (100% of weight) and over a third of the STI (35%) are pure capital-efficiency or shareholder-return metrics; the remaining STI weight (65%) is safety/ESG/cost-efficiency and an undisclosed individual component — not empire-building measures, but also not per-share value metrics. The LTI plan requires the earned amount to be invested in Hydro shares with a **3-year lock-in**, and **Hydro has no share-option scheme** — removing the asymmetric risk-taking incentive that options can create. The LTI is also conditional on the company posting a positive adjusted EBIT in the prior year (a loss-year payout blocker) [Remuneration Report 2025, "LTI performance goals," p.21; "Overview of remuneration elements," p.7].

**2025 LTI outcome shows real teeth, not a rubber stamp:** the RoaCE component paid 68.7% of its potential (3-year average market-value RoaCE of 6.9% — 5.46% in 2023, 6.9% in 2024, 8.3% in 2025 — against the 10% target), but the **TSR component paid zero**: Hydro's cumulative 2023–2025 TSR was +7.6% versus the named peer group's weighted average of +24.1%, a −16.5 percentage-point shortfall that falls below the −5pp minimum threshold for any payout. Blended, the 2025 LTI paid out at 34.3% of maximum potential — NOK 829k for the CEO, equal to 10.3% of his base salary against a 30%-of-base maximum [Remuneration Report 2025, "LTI results for 2025," p.22].

**Redesign in progress.** Following shareholder and proxy-advisor feedback on the FY2024 remuneration report (see §3), the Board is replacing the current backward-looking restricted-share LTI with a forward-looking performance-share plan from the 2027 grant, keeping the same 50%/50% RoaCE/TSR-vs-peer split but shifting the performance period to run *before* vesting rather than being locked in after a historical award — intended to tighten the link between pay and future, not past, shareholder value creation [Remuneration Report 2025, "Revised Long-Term Incentive (LTI) structure — Effective from 2027 grant," p.23].

**CEO's ESG/climate-linked pay is material and separately tracked.** Within the Performance-goal bucket, the report separately discloses that the CEO could earn up to 19.2% of his base salary on ESG-tagged sub-targets (environmental, nature, climate, social, governance, human-rights-in-supply-chain) in 2025 and actually earned 19.0% of base salary against them — a meaningful share of his roughly 44% of base salary in total STI, and distinct from the RoaCE/TSR financial metrics [Remuneration Report 2025, "CEO Compensation linked to ESG targets and achievements," p.21].

## 3. Pay vs Performance

| Signal | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| CEO total pay (latest) | NOK 15,060k (FY2025), up 10.6% from NOK 13,616k in FY2024 | [Remuneration Report 2025, "Total remuneration," p.9] |
| Pay vs peers (if available) | FY2024 CEO total pay of ~NOK 14m sat well **below** the reported median of NOK 38m for other CEOs at Norway Metals & Mining companies with market caps above NOK 83bn — Hydro's own remuneration policy states pay should be "competitive but not market leading," and the outturn is consistent with that stated moderation, reinforced by Norwegian-government pay guidelines applicable given the State's 34.5% ownership | [Web: Simply Wall St, "This Is Why Shareholders May Want To Hold Back On A Pay Rise For Norsk Hydro ASA's (OB:NHY) CEO," dated ~2025 (unverified secondary source, but figures are drawn from the company's own FY2024 remuneration report); Remuneration Report 2025, "Remuneration structure," p.7 and "Dear reader," p.4 (Board Chair's own statement that "CEO compensation was competitive in Norway" but "behind European market levels")] |
| Pay-for-performance alignment | Mixed but with real consequences both ways: FY2024's 39% pay jump drew shareholder criticism because trailing 3-year TSR (2022-2024) was reported as roughly −4.3% and EPS had fallen ~14% over that window; FY2025's 10.6% pay rise came in a year of strong standalone results (Group ARoaCE 10.2% vs. 10% target, TSR +26.9%), yet the LTI's own 3-year TSR-vs-peer component still paid **zero** because the 2023-2025 3-year run underperformed peers by 16.5pp — the mechanism penalized the multi-year shortfall even as the single strong year lifted headline pay | [Web: Simply Wall St, dated ~2025 (unverified secondary, company-report-derived figures); Remuneration Report 2025, "STI results 2025," p.16; "LTI results for 2025," p.22; `management-governance/01_management-and-track-record.md`, ARoaCE 10.2% vs 10% goal] |
| Say-on-pay support (%) | At the 2025 AGM, the Board's Report on Executive Remuneration for **FY2024** was subject to its statutory advisory vote: approximately **74% in favor / 26% against**. Hydro states it responded with a two-phase incentive redesign (simplified STI weighting from 2025; forward-looking LTI from the 2027 grant) in direct response to that feedback. The FY2025 report (this document) was itself put to an advisory vote at the AGM of 7 May 2026, where Hydro's own press release states all Board proposals on the agenda were adopted, but the specific vote split for this item is not disclosed in the sources reviewed | [Remuneration Report 2025, "Dear reader" and "Executive Remuneration Benchmark," p.4; Web: GlobeNewswire, "Norsk Hydro: Minutes from the Annual General Meeting 2026," 2026-05-07 (unverified, dated — confirms adoption but not the line-item vote split)] |

A **26% against** vote on a say-on-pay item is a materially high opposition level (most say-on-pay votes at large-cap companies clear with single-digit-to-low-teens opposition); it is a genuine minority-shareholder signal, not noise, and the Board's own letter treats it as such.

## 4. Incentive Alignment Read

Hydro's pay plan rewards **capital efficiency and relative shareholder return, not scale**: RoaCE (a return-on-capital metric, split between the STI's 35%-weighted financial goal and half of the LTI) and TSR-versus-a-named-peer-group (the other half of the LTI) are the only two financial metrics in the CEO's and CFO's compensation, and neither revenue, absolute EBITDA, acquisition count, nor headcount appears anywhere in the disclosed structure — and the mechanism has real teeth, having paid zero on the LTI's TSR leg for 2023-2025 despite a strong 2025 on its own. The remaining ~65% of the STI (safety/ESG/cost-efficiency scorecards, plus an undisclosed 25% individual component) is not size-chasing either, but it dilutes the purity of the per-share signal and leaves a real disclosure gap on a quarter of annual bonus; combined with heavy fixed-pay weighting (71% for the CEO) and below-peer-median total pay that drew a notable 26% say-on-pay opposition vote on the prior year's report, the picture is one of a deliberately moderated, mostly-returns-based plan rather than an aggressive pay-for-growth one. **Conclusion: well-aligned (returns/per-share)**, with the caveats that the individual-goal weighting is opaque and the plan's teeth were demonstrated on the downside (a zero LTI payout leg) more convincingly than they have yet been tested on unchecked upside.

## Incentive Alignment Score

| Component | Score | Max Score | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Returns / per-share metrics | 18 | 25 | LTI is 100% RoaCE/TSR (returns-based); STI's financial goal (RoaCE) is 35% of the CEO's bonus; but the majority of STI weight (65%) is safety/ESG/individual, and returns-linked pay was only ~41% of the CEO's *earned* variable pay in FY2025 (Findings 03-004, 03-005, 03-007, 03-008) |
| Metric clarity and weights | 16 | 20 | Full numeric weights and thresholds disclosed for STI and LTI, with a linear payout formula for RoaCE and an explicit TSR band; the 25%-weighted individual-goal component is not disclosed (Findings 03-004 through 03-006, 03-011) |
| Pay-for-performance alignment | 14 | 20 | LTI's TSR leg paid zero for 3-year peer underperformance despite a strong FY2025 alone; but FY2024's 39% pay rise amid weak 3-year TSR/EPS drew a 26% say-on-pay opposition vote (Findings 03-009, 03-012, 03-013) |
| Long-term orientation | 12 | 15 | 3-year share lock-in, no options, EBIT-positive payout gate, and a shift to a forward-looking performance-share design from the 2027 grant (Findings 03-009, 03-014, 03-015) |
| Pay magnitude vs peers/performance | 8 | 10 | CEO total pay (~NOK 14-15m) sits below the disclosed Norway Metals & Mining peer median of NOK 38m; consistent with stated "not market leading" policy (Finding 03-013) |
| Minority-holder alignment | 7 | 10 | No dilutive options, real share ownership with claw-back provisions, and state-linked pay-moderation guidelines constrain excess; offset by the opacity on individual goals and the 26% say-on-pay opposition (Findings 03-006, 03-012, 03-015, 03-018) |
| **Total** | **75** | **100** | — |

Governance-Rating band for this score: 61-80 = Strong. No score-cap rule from the "no proxy/compensation disclosure" table is applied here because the actual proxy-equivalent document (the Remuneration Report 2025) was obtained and read in full, with individual figures and weights confirmed to the source's own page numbers (see §0).

## 4. Control Structure

| Feature | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Dual-class / super-voting | None. "Hydro has one share class with equal rights for all shareholders" — one vote per share, no super-voting instrument, and the State's shares carry "no preferential voting rights." | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §4 "Equal treatment of shareholders," p.293; Note 9.1, p.198] |
| Controlled-company status | Not a formally "controlled company" under any single-majority test (no holder exceeds 50%), but the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries' 34.26–34.49% stake is a **blocking minority** under Norwegian company law (many special resolutions require a two-thirds majority of votes cast), and combined with Folketrygdfondet's 7.3% state-linked stake, state-affiliated holders control ~41.8% of the register — the single largest bloc by a wide margin over the next holder (BlackRock/Vanguard, each under 5%). | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, Note 9.1, p.198; NUES Report, p.293]; [NorskHydroASAOBNHY_PublicCompany.pdf, Top Holders, 2026-07-18] |
| Shareholder bloc with board rights | The State has no charter-level board-nomination right disclosed; Board members are elected by the General Meeting via the Nomination Committee under ordinary process. However, the NUES Report explicitly carves out a Section-14 (Takeover) deviation "due to the Norwegian state['s]... ownership of 34.26 percent," meaning the Board has NOT adopted general takeover-defense principles because the State's blocking stake already functions as a de facto takeover deterrent — a real, if informal, control-rights effect of the stake's size. | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §14 "Takeovers," p.293: "The Board has not established general principles for handling takeover bids due to the Norwegian state['s]... ownership of 34.26 percent"] |
| Controlling-owner objective alignment *(Filter 6)* | **Government control test trips.** The Ministry describes its stake in Hydro via Norway's "Active Ownership Report" (Report to the Storting no. 6, 2022-2023) as held for "a long-term ownership perspective... for the purpose of retaining a leading technology and industrial company with head office functions in Norway" — an explicit industrial-policy / jobs-and-headquarters objective, not a stated per-share-value-maximization mandate. This is the textbook Filter 6(a) government-control conflict: the controlling shareholder pursues national-strategic objectives (keeping HQ functions and technology in Norway) that can diverge from a minority holder's pure return objective. | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §14, p.293: "the Active Ownership Report (Report to the Storting no. 6 (2022-2023))... expressed a long-term ownership perspective in the company for the purpose of retaining a leading technology and industrial company with head office functions in Norway... p.44"] |

**Unaligned-owner test (CLAUDE.md §24, Filter 6) — RF-OWN-004 triggered.** The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries' 34.26–34.49% stake is government control per Filter 6(a): the State's own disclosed rationale for holding the stake is industrial/employment policy (retaining head-office functions and technology in Norway), not per-share value creation. This is a structural cap on shareholder-friendliness, not a discount to arbitrage — a stock trading cheap under this ownership structure can stay cheap indefinitely because the controlling holder is not selling into strength, forcing capital discipline, or pushing for a re-rating; it is holding for national-strategic reasons. That said, two mitigants are disclosed and should not be discarded: (1) there is no preferential voting right and one share class, so the State cannot extract value through differential voting power; (2) the State's own buyback participation was capped to keep its percentage stake exactly flat (34.26%) rather than let its influence creep up via non-participation in a shrinking share count — a small positive signal that it is not using the buyback mechanism to increase control cheaply. Net: the government-control conflict is real and structural, but it is a "hold for strategic reasons" risk (patient, non-extractive) rather than a "hold to loot/self-deal" risk — Note 9.1's related-party transactions with the State-linked ecosystem (Statkraft/DNB/wind-JV power purchases) are individually small (~NOK 428m combined vs NOK 207,971m FY2025 revenue) and disclosed at arm's length. **Persistent cheapness under this ownership structure should be read by the valuation module as a possible value trap, not a margin of safety, until there is direct evidence the State would support or vote for value-accretive corporate actions (buybacks, M&A, structural change) against its stated jobs/HQ mandate.**

## 5. Ownership / Insider Read

Executives bought their stake through a Long-Term Incentive program that requires them to invest net proceeds in Hydro shares and hold for three years — a real purchase mechanism, not a pure grant — but the resulting personal holdings are tiny in percentage terms: the CEO's 111,605 shares and the CFO's 23,659 shares, plus the rest of the Board and Executive Leadership Team, add up to roughly 0.027% of the company, so there is essentially no insider ownership signal to read either way. There is no pool record of open-market insider buying or selling in the last 12 months (only a web-sourced, unverified, plan-based purchase in April 2026, which does not count as a red flag or a conviction signal under this module's rules), and no pledging by the State or any director is disclosed anywhere. The biggest structural fact for minority holders is not insider behavior — it is that the Norwegian state, through the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries, controls 34.26–34.49% of the company for an explicitly stated industrial-policy purpose (keeping head-office functions and technology in Norway), not for per-share value maximization; that single fact, not management's modest personal stake, is the dominant ownership risk this module can identify.

## management-governance / 05_board-and-shareholder-rights.md

# Board & Shareholder Rights — NHY

## 1. Board Composition

| Feature | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Board size | 11 members as of 31 Dec 2025: 7 shareholder-elected (all classed independent) + 4 employee-representative directors | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §8, p.295: "the Board had 11 members. Seven are elected by the General Meeting. Four are elected by employees in Norway"] |
| Independent directors (%) | 100% of the 7 shareholder-elected directors are deemed independent of executive management and material business relationships; counting the full 11-seat board (including the 4 employee-representative directors, who are not classed "independent" under the Norwegian code but are also not executives), the ratio is 7/11 = 63.6% | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §8, p.295: "All shareholder elected members were deemed to be independent under Norwegian standards in 2025"] |
| Chair / CEO split? | Yes, fully split. Chair: Rune Bjerke (non-executive, former Group CEO of DNB Bank ASA, director since 2020, Chair since May 2024). CEO: Eivind Kallevik (executive, in role since May 2024). The Chair is one of the shareholder-elected independent directors, not a company insider | [Norsk Hydro ASA OB NHY Board Members export, "Bjerke, Rune"; management-governance/01_management-and-track-record.md, §1] |
| Audit / Comp / Nominating committee independence | **Audit Committee** (4 members: Marianne Wiinholt — Chair, Philip New, Espen Gundersen, Bjørn Petter Moxnes): 3 of 4 are independent shareholder-elected directors; the 4th, Moxnes, is an employee-representative director, and the filing itself footnotes that his participation is a reliance the company judges does not "adversely affect... the ability of the Board Audit Committee to act independently." **People & Remuneration Committee** (3 members: Rune Bjerke — Chair, Kristin Fejerskov Kragseth, Arve Baade): 2 of 3 independent, 1 employee-representative (Baade). **Nomination Committee**: elected by the General Meeting, independent of the Board and management by design, but the Norwegian state (Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries) and the Government Pension Fund Norway (Folketrygdfondet) — Hydro's two largest shareholders — each hold a seat on it directly (Muriel Bjørseth Hansen for the Ministry, Karl Mathisen for Folketrygdfondet) | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §7 and §9, p.294-296] |

Both board committees that oversee financial integrity and executive pay (Audit; People & Remuneration) include one employee-representative director apiece. This is the standard Norwegian co-determination model, not a related-party conflict — employee representatives have no executive authority and no equity comp exposure of their own — but it means these two committees are not 100% independent-director bodies in the stricter sense used in some other regimes (e.g., the US SEC's fully-independent audit-committee requirement).

## 2. Tenure & Refreshment

| Signal | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Average director tenure | Shareholder-elected directors average ~4.1 years on the Board (Bjerke 6 yrs since 2020; Kragseth 4 yrs since 2022; Wiinholt 10 yrs since 2016; Gundersen 2 yrs since 2024; New 4 yrs since 2022; Toogood 2 yrs since 2024; Wahl 1 yr since 2025) | [Norsk Hydro ASA OB NHY Board Members export, individual "Years on Board" fields] |
| Overboarding / staleness signs | Marianne Wiinholt, Chair of the Audit Committee, is the longest-tenured shareholder-elected director at 10 years (since 2016) — long enough that some codes (e.g., the UK Corporate Governance Code's 9-year guideline) would flag a fresh independence review, though the Norwegian NUES code carries no such numeric tenure trigger and the company states she remains independent. Separately, two directors carry a meaningfully heavier concurrent board load: Kim Wahl sits on ~5 other boards/foundations (Aspelin Ramm Gruppen, Fristads Kansas, Kavli Holding, Vend Marketplaces, Voxtra Foundation) alongside Hydro, and Espen Gundersen sits on 4 other listed/private boards (Hexagon Purus, Kid ASA — as Chair, Scatec ASA, Compac Sorting Equipment) alongside Hydro and his Hydro Audit Committee seat | [Norsk Hydro ASA OB NHY Board Members export, "Other Boards" fields for Wahl and Gundersen] |
| Recent refreshment | 3 of the 7 shareholder-elected directors joined within the last 2 years: Espen Gundersen and Jane Toogood (both May 2024) and Kim Wahl (May 2025) — a genuine one-third-plus refresh of the shareholder-elected bench in two AGM cycles | [Norsk Hydro ASA OB NHY Board Members export; integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §8] |

Refreshment is real (three new shareholder-elected directors in two years), which offsets the single long-tenured Audit Committee chair. The overboarding signal on Wahl and Gundersen is a monitoring item, not disqualifying — most of their other seats are private-company or foundation boards with lighter workloads than a second large-cap listed board, but Gundersen also chairs Kid ASA, which adds meaningful time commitment on top of his Hydro Audit Committee seat.

## 3. Related-Party Transactions & Group Leakage

| RPT Type | Amount | % of Revenue | % of PAT | % of Net Worth | Arm's Length? | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Power purchases from Hydro Rein-related JV entities (Sweden wind, Brazil wind) | NOK 428m (NOK 64m + NOK 42m Sweden, NOK 322m Brazil, FY2025) | 0.21% | 6.4% | 0.4% | Yes — "at fixed prices subject to inflation adjustment" under long-term power purchase agreements; company states "transactions with related parties are at arm's length principles" | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, Note 9.1, p.198] |
| Rent and related services paid to Norsk Hydros Pensjonskasse (Hydro's own pension trust) | NOK 98m (FY2025) vs NOK 94m (FY2024) | 0.05% | 1.5% | 0.09% | Yes — priced on 2006/2015 market-benchmarked rates, per a rental arrangement whose current term expires Feb 2027 | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, Note 9.1, p.198] |
| Electricity sold to the pension trust / administrative-cost reimbursements to/from the pension trust | NOK 6m electricity sale + ~NOK 26m combined admin/service reimbursements (FY2025) | 0.02% | 0.5% | 0.03% | Yes — services at cost reimbursement, standard trust-administration arrangement | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, Note 9.1, p.198] |
| Norwegian State as related party (34.5% shareholder, Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries) — general business dealings with state-controlled entities (e.g., power from Statkraft, banking from DNB) | Not separately quantified; Board states these are "agreed independently of the possible control exercised by the State" | Not quantified | Not quantified | Not quantified | Company-asserted arm's length; no preferential pricing or terms disclosed | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, Note 9.1, p.198] |
| Outstanding receivables from related parties (pension trust) | NOK 4m receivable / NOK 6m payable to the pension trust, both settled early 2026 | Immaterial | Immaterial | Immaterial | Yes | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, Note 9.1, p.198] |

Total disclosed related-party flows sum to roughly NOK 558 million against FY2025 revenue of NOK 207,971 million — about **0.27% of revenue**, well inside the Low materiality band (<1% of revenue/assets) under the module's thresholds. The Board explicitly states: "no material transactions occurred in 2025 between the group and its shareholders, Board members, Executive Leadership Team or related parties" beyond the items itemized above [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §9, p.296]. These RPTs are recurring, small, and disclosed as arm's length; `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan.md` independently confirmed the >25%-of-revenue/expenses hard disqualifier does not trigger (computed ratio well under 1%). Hydro's joint-venture partners (e.g., Qatalum, 50% joint venture with Qatar Petroleum) are explicitly **not** treated as related parties — the company classifies them as competitors in other dealings, a reasonable IFRS-consistent distinction, though it is worth noting as the one judgment call in the RPT boundary. No promoter-style leakage channel exists in this ownership structure: there is no controlling family or promoter group extracting royalties, management fees, or rent — the largest shareholder is a state ministry with a disclosed hands-off policy on day-to-day operations.

**Read:** No material related-party leakage to a controlling insider. This is a structural strength relative to promoter-controlled peers in other jurisdictions.

## 4. Takeover Defenses & Voting Rights

| Feature | Present? | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Poison pill | No | "Hydro's Articles of Association and underlying governing documents contain no defense mechanisms against acquisition offers, and no measures have been implemented to restrict the acquisition of shares in the company" | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §14, p.297] |
| Classified / staggered board | Not disclosed as staggered | Shareholder-elected directors serve terms of up to two years, but the NUES Report describes no staggered-class structure (all shareholder-elected seats appear subject to periodic re-election as a group, not split into rotating classes) | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §8, p.296] |
| Dual-class / unequal voting | No | "Hydro has one share class with equal rights for all shareholders" and "there are no different voting rights associated with the shares outstanding"; the Norwegian State's 34.5% stake carries "no preferential voting rights" | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §4-5, p.294; Note 9.1, p.198] |
| Majority vs plurality director voting | Not disclosed in the pool | The filing does not state whether director elections use a majority-of-votes-cast standard versus plurality; this is a genuine data gap for this specific mechanic | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §6, p.294-295 — general voting process described, standard not specified] |
| Shareholder ability to call meetings / act by written consent | Partial disclosure | The filing confirms shareholders may submit written proposals for agenda items/resolutions at least four weeks before the ordinary General Meeting. It does not restate the statutory Norwegian Companies Act threshold for shareholders to demand an extraordinary general meeting; that is a matter of Norwegian company law generally, not company-specific disclosure in this filing — **not confirmed from this pool, treated as a data gap rather than assumed** | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §6, p.294] |

**One deviation worth flagging on its own:** the Board has explicitly declined to adopt the NUES-recommended practice of establishing "general principles for handling takeover bids," and states this is specifically **because of the Norwegian state's 34.26% ownership stake** — implying the Board itself judges a contested takeover to be impractical given the state's blocking position, rather than because Hydro has installed its own defenses [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, NUES Report §14, p.297: "The Board has not established general principles for handling takeover bids due to the Norwegian state... ownership of 34.26 percent of the Hydro shares"]. This means the practical takeover-defense mechanism at Hydro is not a poison pill or staggered board — it is the sheer size of the state's stake, which also functions as a blocking minority (above the roughly one-third threshold) against special resolutions requiring a two-thirds majority under Norwegian company law (e.g., mergers, capital-structure changes, Articles amendments). This is disclosed, not hidden, but it is a real structural constraint on any change-of-control outcome that the state's Ministry does not support.

The May 7, 2026 AGM (covering the FY2025 dividend proposal and a management-remuneration-report advisory vote) had already occurred by this report's 2026-07-19 as-of date, but its results are likewise absent from the pool | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, "The Hydro share," p.2959: "A total of 80.02 percent of the voting share capital was represented"; management-governance/00_governance-data-triage.md, row "AGM voting"] |

**Read:** dilution risk is low and the share count trend favors existing holders, but the total absence of AGM vote-tally data is a real transparency gap for this specific test — the module cannot confirm whether any resolution (director election, remuneration policy, auditor reappointment) drew meaningful shareholder opposition in 2025 or 2026. This caps the "AGM opposition / minority protection" score component below (§ score table) rather than being scored on assumed clean data.

## 5. Minority-Shareholder Protection Read

The architecture is genuinely shareholder-friendly on paper: one share class with equal voting rights, no poison pill, no staggered board, no preferential voting for the state, a fully split Chair/CEO structure, a majority-independent shareholder-elected board bench that has refreshed three of seven seats in the last two years, and related-party dealings that are small (about 0.27% of revenue), recurring, and explicitly attested as arm's length by the Board — none of the promoter-style leakage risk that shows up in controlled-company structures elsewhere applies here. The single biggest structural risk to minority holders is not board entrenchment in the usual sense — it is that the Norwegian state's ~34.3-34.5% stake is large enough to function as a blocking minority over major corporate-law resolutions and large enough that Hydro's own Board has declined to even draft takeover-bid-handling principles, citing the state's position as the reason a contested change of control is not realistically on the table; the state's stated rationale for holding the stake ("retaining a leading technology and industrial company with head office functions in Norway," per the Storting Active Ownership Report) is a national-strategic objective, not a per-share-value mandate, and that gap between the controlling shareholder's goal and a per-share-value goal is the item `04_ownership-and-insider-behavior` should test directly against CLAUDE.md §24 Filter 6 (structurally unaligned controlling owner) — this agent flags the fact pattern but does not itself apply that filter's score cap, since `04_ownership-and-insider-behavior` cross-module input is not available at time of this report (parallel layer, not yet run). A second, more contained gap is that the pool contains no AGM vote-tally data for either the 2025 or 2026 meeting, so opposition levels on pay, RPT, or director resolutions cannot be checked. On the evidence actually in hand, this reads as **adequate** protection: the mechanical rights (one share/one vote, no defenses, clean RPT, independent-majority board) are real and verified, but the concentration of a strategically-motivated 34%+ shareholder and the missing voting-transparency data mean the read stops short of "strong."

*Cross-module note for `99_management-governance-synthesis`:* if `04_ownership-and-insider-behavior` independently concludes the Norwegian state's stake and stated national-strategic mandate meet the RF-OWN-004 bar (structurally unaligned controlling owner, CLAUDE.md §24 Filter 6), the synthesis should apply the associated Shareholder friendliness cap (max 55) and Governance risk floor (55) per the Score Cap Rules, and treat this module's minority-protection read as no better than "weak / entrenched" on that basis, superseding the "adequate" conclusion reached here on the board-mechanics evidence alone.

# Candor & Disclosure Quality — NHY

Norsk Hydro ASA reports under IFRS Accounting Standards as adopted by the EU, in Norwegian Krone (NOK), fiscal year ending 31 December [Integrated Annual Report 2025, p.140]. This agent uses two **verbatim** earnings-call transcripts in the data pool — the FQ4 2025 call (2026-02-13) and the FQ1 2026 call (2026-04-29), both S&P Global Market Intelligence-transcribed records of management's own words and analyst Q&A — so the partial-data cap for "no transcripts" does NOT apply here. `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md` is present and used as the non-GAAP cross-check, so that cap also does not apply.

## 1. Owning the Misses

| Miss (from 01) | How It Was Communicated | Owned or Obscured? | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 Recycling/Extrusions EBITDA growth-pillar targets not reached; some 2030 targets postponed | Stated in management's own words on the investor-day scorecard slide ("2025 EBITDA targets not reached; 2030 targets postponed") and repeated in the CEO's annual-report letter ("challenges made us fall short of the 2025 targets, and we have postponed some of the 2030 targets") — the metric itself was not redefined or dropped after the miss | **Owned** — plain language, no reframing of the KPI | [nhy-investor-day-2025.pdf, p.6; integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, "Letter to stakeholders," p.5] |
| FY2025 capex guidance cut mid-year by NOK 1.5bn vs the original NOK 15bn plan | Disclosed explicitly in the CEO's own letter as a deliberate response ("we reduced our capex guiding for 2025 by NOK 1.5 billion to adapt to market realities"), not a silent underspend against an unrevised number | **Owned** — the revision itself, and its cause, are named | [integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, "Letter to stakeholders," p.4] |
| FQ4 2025: reported EBITDA of ~NOK 2bn vs adjusted EBITDA of NOK 5.6bn; reported net loss of NOK (2.2)bn vs adjusted net income of NOK 1.7bn — the weakest reported quarter in the pool | CFO walked through every adjusting item live on the call with exact NOK figures (unrealized LME derivative loss NOK 2.3bn, rationalization/closure costs NOK 1.3bn, impairments NOK 700m) rather than citing only the adjusted headline. The CEO's opening remarks also named the "difficult but necessary restructuring decisions" (workforce reduction, 5 extrusion-plant closures) driving the quarter, without euphemism-only framing | **Owned** — the reported (GAAP) loss and its exact drivers were stated, not skipped past in favor of the adjusted number alone | [Norsk Hydro ASA, Q4 2025 Earnings Call transcript, 2026-02-13, Presentation section, CFO remarks] |
| Q1 2026: negative free cash flow of NOK (4)bn despite a strong adjusted EBITDA beat | The CEO led his own highlights paragraph with it — "operating capital is also higher, resulting in a negative free cash flow of NOK 4 billion" — placed in the same breath as the EBITDA beat, not omitted or pushed to a later slide | **Owned** — negative cash flow was volunteered in the opening highlights, not buried | [Norsk Hydro ASA, Q1 2026 Earnings Call transcript, 2026-04-29, Presentation section] |
| Fatal contractor incident at the Alunorte refinery (30 March 2026) | CEO opened the Q1 2026 call with it directly, before any financial content: "we are deeply saddened by the passing of a contractor... if the investigation concludes that inadequate safety measures contributed to this incident, we will, of course, take this extremely seriously." No minimization, no deflection to "the investigation will clarify" as a way to avoid commitment | **Owned** — led the call, plain acknowledgment of possible fault pending investigation | [Norsk Hydro ASA, Q1 2026 Earnings Call transcript, 2026-04-29, Presentation section] |
| Consensus EPS misses in FQ3 2025 (−12.8%) and FQ4 2025 (−6.8%) | No formal group EPS guidance exists to miss (confirmed in `earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md`, §2), so this is a Street-consensus miss, not a broken company promise; the underlying drivers (lower alumina prices, extrusion headwinds, restructuring costs) were explained in full on both calls with itemized bridges, not glossed over | **Owned** at the level of explaining the drivers — but not a "promise miss" since no formal EPS target existed to break | [earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md, §6; Q4 2025 and Q3 2025 transcript presentation sections] |

## 2. Non-GAAP / Adjustment Aggressiveness

| Signal | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Recurring "one-off" addbacks | "Significant rationalization and closure costs" have been added back to EBITDA/EBIT every year for three straight years and the amount is growing, not shrinking: NOK 265m (FY2023) → NOK 407m (FY2024) → NOK 1,795m (FY2025). A goodwill/PP&E impairment has also been booked every year (NOK 4,424m / 22m / 1,069m). The module's own earnings-quality rule treats a charge that recurs every period as not genuinely one-off | earnings/06, §4–§5, §8 (Accounting Trap Checklist, severity 60/100 for recurring restructuring) |
| GAAP-to-adjusted gap (magnitude / trend) | The gap is modest and sign-flipping at the EBITDA line (−4.4% FY2023, −0.8% FY2024, +12.4% FY2025) but large and **directionally consistent every year** at net income/EPS: reported net income sat below the company's own adjusted figure by +34% (FY2025), +84% (FY2024), and +180% (FY2023). This is the single largest reported-vs-adjusted divergence earnings/06 identifies for Hydro | earnings/06, §7 (Reported vs Adjusted Reconciliation), §10 |
| Does adjusted framing flatter reality? | Partially. At EBITDA, the adjusted figure is a fair operating read (the swings are structural, non-cash derivative-timing effects). At net income and EPS, the adjusted figure is persistently and materially higher than reported, driven by impairments and the recurring rationalization add-back — a reader who anchors on adjusted EPS alone (e.g. NOK 4.26 adjusted vs NOK 1.77 reported in FY2023) gets a rosier read of that year than the audited bottom line supports. The company discloses the full reconciliation and it is audited — this is a disclosed-but-persistent framing bias, not concealment, and earnings/06 scored overall earnings quality 55/100 ("mixed... material concerns from recurring one-off charges") on this exact pattern | earnings/06, §7, §9, §10 |

## 3. Disclosure Transparency

Segment-level disclosure is genuinely granular: each quarter management gives a five-segment (Bauxite & Alumina, Aluminium Metal, Metal Markets, Extrusions, Energy) forward bridge with quantified NOK/USD cost and price ranges — e.g. the FQ1 2026 call gave specific figures such as "67% of Q2 primary production booked at USD 3,000/tonne," "carbon costs expected to increase NOK 150-250 million," and "fixed costs NOK 300-400 million higher" — well beyond boilerplate segment commentary [Q1 2026 transcript, presentation section]. One disclosure gap has persisted rather than improved: Hydro still does not split maintenance ("sustaining") capex from growth capex in the data pool, despite qualitatively flagging "historically high sustaining capital expenditure," which forces this module's free-cash-flow read to use total capex as a blunter proxy [earnings/06, §1, footnote 3; integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf, p.51]. No evidence was found of any KPI or segment disclosure becoming *less* transparent over time — if anything the quarter-over-quarter cost/price bridges have become more numerically specific across the two transcripts reviewed.

## 4. Tone in Bad Times

The worst reported quarter in the pool is FQ4 2025 (reported net loss of NOK (2.2)bn, EPS consensus miss of −6.8%, negative Extrusions EBITDA, plant closures and a workforce reduction). The CEO's tone was matter-of-fact rather than promotional — he named the restructuring as "difficult but necessary" and did not use language claiming strength where the numbers showed weakness. In Q&A, analysts asked pointed, specific questions (extrusion order-book visibility for H2 2026, whether the strong B&A trading result was sustainable, the drivers of the fixed-cost increase) and received direct numeric answers each time (e.g., "around NOK 300 million in very strong commercial results in B&A in Q4") rather than deflection to "we'll follow up offline." The one genuinely evasive-sounding answer — on whether extrusion volumes would recover in H2 2026 — was an honest "too early to conclude" rather than a confident but unsupported forecast, which is itself a candor-consistent response to real forward uncertainty rather than spin.

## 5. Candor Read

Management owns its misses in plain language: it wrote "2025 EBITDA targets not reached; 2030 targets postponed" on its own investor-day slide, led its Q1 2026 highlights with a negative free-cash-flow number rather than hiding it behind an EBITDA beat, and opened a call with a fatal workplace incident before any financial content. Q&A across both verbatim transcripts shows analysts getting specific, numeric answers rather than deflection. The one real soft spot is non-GAAP discipline — a "rationalization and closure cost" that has been added back as non-recurring every year for three years, growing each time, and a net-income/EPS gap versus the adjusted figure that has run from +34% to +180% across FY2023–FY2025 — fully disclosed and audited, but a persistent pattern that flatters the adjusted bottom line versus the reported one. No unresolved adverse integrity signal was routed from `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` (confirmed in `01_management-and-track-record.md`, §4A), so there is no compounding integrity concern to weigh against this read. On balance: **candid / high-trust**, with the qualifier that reported net income/EPS should never be read standalone given the scale and persistence of the adjusted-vs-reported gap.

## valuation — module synthesis

_Source: `valuation/99_valuation-synthesis.md`_

# Valuation Module — NHY (Synthesis)

## Abstract

Norsk Hydro screens as fairly valued, not cheap: the triangulated base-case fair value of NOK 81.83 per share sits 3.7% below the NOK 84.96 price (2026-07-17, pool-verified), inside the ±10% "fairly valued" band. Bull is NOK 107.70 (+26.8%, requires the current Middle East supply-shock margin and multiple to both persist), Bear is NOK 45.12 (−46.9%, a structural, not cyclical, impairment of Hydro's upstream cost-curve advantage and Extrusions), and sum-of-the-parts — the most tightly reconciled method, tying within 0.3% of consolidated enterprise value — drives the base. The price implies Hydro's margin holds near its FY2025 actual (13.9%) rather than fading to the DCF's 13.0% mid-cycle anchor, a stretch two earnings modules call non-durable. There is no margin of safety today (−3.8% cushion); the real asymmetry is 46.9% downside to the bear case against 26.8% upside to bull. A structurally misaligned controlling owner (the Norwegian State, 34.5%) means any apparent peer-relative discount cannot be read as a clean re-rating case — this is fair value with real downside skew, not a bargain.

## 1. Valuation Verdict

- **Verdict:** Fairly valued
- **Base-case fair value (point, per share):** NOK 81.83 [`07_scenario-and-fair-value.md` §2]
- **Current price:** NOK 84.96, as of 2026-07-17 (last close, pool-verified) [`01_price-and-capital-structure.md` §1]
- **Bull / Base / Bear fair-value levels (points):** Bull NOK 107.70 (+26.8% vs price) / Base NOK 81.83 (−3.7% vs price) / Bear NOK 45.12 (−46.9% vs price, structural reset — headline) [`07` §3]
- **Cross-method dispersion (football field, low–high):** Weighted-method base points cluster NOK 70.14 (intrinsic DCF) to NOK 93.70 (peer relative), a 33.6% spread — under the 40% "must-lead-with-it" threshold but the central reconciliation question. The wider internal-sensitivity extremes (DCF sensitivity floor NOK 52.51 to full peer-parity ceiling NOK 134.10) are shown for transparency only and are not treated as the decision-relevant dispersion [`07` §2]. SOTP's own named-comparable range is NOK 78.27–106.47.
- Valuation attractiveness /100 *(higher = cheaper)*: **38** — the base case shows price sitting slightly *above*, not below, fair value (−3.7% implied upside); further capped at max 60 by the RF-OWN-004 unaligned-owner flag, but the actual read is well under that ceiling
- Margin of safety /100 *(higher = better)*: **30** — cushion is negative (−3.83%): price is priced above, not below, the base-case fair value
- Valuation confidence /100: **56** — capped at max 60 by DCF terminal dominance (terminal value = 78.1% of DCF EV); further tempered by the pervasive Capital IQ EBITDA/EBIT reclassification error (flagged and corrected downstream, but a real cross-check burden) and a discretionary FX/quality-discount stack in the peer method
- Downside risk /100 *(higher = WORSE)*: **68** — 46.9% distance from price to the bear-case (structural-reset) value is a large, real downside
- Data quality /100: **75** — comprehensive pool (price, consensus, peers, segments, cash flow all present and dated), tempered by the material CIQ vendor EBITDA/EBIT mismatch that every specialist had to independently detect and correct
- Overall usefulness /100: **79**
- Dominant valuation method (one line): Sum-of-the-parts (40% weight) — built entirely on Hydro's own audited segment Adjusted EBITDA disclosures, and its gross enterprise value ties within 0.3% of the consolidated canonical EV bridge, the least forecasting judgment of any method here [`06_sum-of-the-parts.md` §4]
- What's priced in (one line): The market is pricing Hydro's FY2025 actual Adjusted EBITDA margin (13.9%) holding roughly flat through FY2030 and into perpetuity — not growth (implied 5-year FCF CAGR −3.21%) — a "Stretch, tilting aggressive" ask that two upstream earnings modules independently call non-durable [`05_reverse-dcf.md` §5]
- Biggest valuation risk (one line): The moat's own eroding trajectory (Extrusions EBIT margin −2.2% in 2025, five plants proposed for closure; upstream cost-curve advantage exposed to Chinese/Gulf capacity growth) drives the 46.9%-downside structural bear case, and is a live possibility per the business-model module, not a tail risk [`07` §3, structural down-leg]

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation

- **Strongest bear point:** The reverse-DCF shows the price already requires Hydro's *elevated* FY2025 margin (13.9%) to persist rather than fade to the DCF's own 13.0% mid-cycle anchor — a real, not trivial, ask that two upstream earnings modules independently flag as resting on a non-durable Middle East supply shock, while the company's own forward hedge book (67% of Q2 2026 volume booked below spot) already partially discounts reversion [`05_reverse-dcf.md` §3, §5].
- **Strongest bull point:** On the multiples independently verified clean (NTM EV/EBITDA, EV/Sales, forward P/E — all cross-checked against consensus and audited figures, not the corrupted CIQ vendor LTM basis), NHY trades an 18%–35% discount to its peer median despite a materially lower leverage profile and a mid-pack-to-superior restated EBITDA margin, implying a NOK 93.70 relative-value base case (+10.2% vs price) even after a conservative 10% quality discount [`03_relative-valuation-peers.md` §3–§5].
- **Single killer risk:** Confirmed (not merely unproven) moat erosion — Hydro Extrusions' EBIT margin fell from ~4% (2020–2023) to −2.2% (2025) with five European plants proposed for closure, and the business-model module's own competitive-intensity read calls a mid-cost-curve upstream competitor within a few years "a live possibility, not a tail risk" [`07_scenario-and-fair-value.md`, structural down-leg, citing `business-model/09_moat.md`, `business-model/07_business-quality.md`].
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** SOTP — the most tightly-reconciled method — ties within 0.3% of the consolidated EV bridge using only audited segment data and sits essentially at the current price (−0.4%), meaning there is no proven variant perception of a hidden segment being mispriced by the market; this argues against the peer method's +10.2% read being an easy, closable gap [`06_sum-of-the-parts.md` §5].

## 2. Specialist Roll-Up

| Specialist | Verdict Line | Biggest Finding |
|---|---|---|
| valuation-data-triage | Sufficient — all five valuation methods can run, no active partial-data caps | Only a minor completeness gap (no discrete dilution schedule); everything else needed for price, DCF, peers, SOTP, and reverse-DCF is present and dated |
| price-and-capital-structure | Price pool-verified at NOK 84.96 (2026-07-17); canonical EV NOK 192,384mm, net debt NOK 17,919mm (cash-quality adjusted) | The headline Capital IQ cash figure includes NOK 4,829mm the company itself says is unavailable to service debt (captive insurance + derivatives collateral) — using the adjusted, not headline, EV/net-debt is canonical for every downstream agent |
| multiples-own-history | Own-history read is illustrative-only (13-month history, well short of the 3-year bar) — zero-weighted in `07` | The trailing "re-rating" (LTM P/E at the 85th percentile of its own short range) is a mechanical artifact of a depressed Q4 2025 earnings trough, not a genuine business re-rating; NTM P/E sits at only the 15th percentile of the same window |
| relative-valuation-peers | NOK 93.70 base case (+10.2% vs price) on a quality-adjusted NTM EV/EBITDA of 5.6x; dispersion NOK 72–134 | The raw vendor LTM EV/EBITDA/EBIT screen shows a spurious ~49%–52% discount — a Capital IQ reclassification error specific to Hydro's IFRS format; restated on audited figures, those same multiples flip to a *premium* |
| intrinsic-dcf | NOK 70.14 base case (−17.4% vs price); sensitivity grid NOK 52.51–102.81 | Terminal value is 78.1% of EV — terminal-dominated and low-confidence by the module's own rule — with a structural runoff terminal (moat-erosion trigger) producing NOK 45.12/share, the input for `07`'s headline bear |
| reverse-dcf | Price implies −3.21% 5-yr FCF CAGR, or a uniform 14.02% Adjusted EBITDA margin held through FY2030+ | The undemanding-looking growth ask is misleading in isolation — the more reliable margin-based solve shows the price needs the FY2025 actual margin (13.9%) to hold, not fade to the DCF's 13.0% mid-cycle anchor — a Stretch, not a Yes |
| sum-of-the-parts | NOK 84.63 base case (−0.4% vs price); dispersion NOK 78.27–106.47 | Aluminium Metal (primary smelting) carries 58.7% of gross enterprise value on only 7.1% of group revenue — the upstream-margin concentration pattern; gross EV ties to the consolidated canonical EV within 0.3% |
| scenario-and-fair-value | Weighted base NOK 81.83 (−3.7% vs price); Bull NOK 107.70 / Bear NOK 45.12 (headline, structural) | Margin of safety is negative (−3.83%); downside to bear is 46.89% — an asymmetric risk/reward the master synthesizer must weigh, not a cushion |

## 3. Reconciliation

The three weighted, value-producing methods disagree by 33.6% at the base-case level — DCF NOK 70.14 (low) to peer relative NOK 93.70 (high), with SOTP NOK 84.63 in between — under the module's 40% "must-lead-with-it" threshold, so this is not an unreconciled disagreement requiring a hard confidence cap on its own, but it is the central question this report resolves. `07`'s own reconciliation judgement is adopted here: SOTP is trusted most (40% weight) because it rests entirely on Hydro's own audited segment disclosures and ties within 0.3% of the consolidated canonical EV — the least forecasting judgment of the three. DCF is trusted second (35% weight) as the Business-Type Method Map's mandated primary method for a commodity/cyclical name, but its terminal-value dominance (78.1% of EV) and wide WACC/g sensitivity earn it real, not top, weight. Peer relative valuation is trusted least (25% weight) because its NOK 93.70 base case stacks two of this report's own judgment calls — an inferred NOK/USD 9.63 FX rate and a discretionary 10% quality discount — on top of an imperfect comp set (only RUSAL, Chalco, and Hindalco are Hydro's own named peers). The own-history multiples method (`02`) is excluded from the weighted blend entirely, per its own "illustrative-only" flag on a 13-month history. Methods broadly agree once weighted — fair value clusters at **NOK 81.83**, dispersion **NOK 70.14–93.70** (weighted-method base points) / **NOK 45.12–107.70** (bull/base/bear scenario levels).

|---|---|---|---|
| No pool-verified price (price-state `indicative` or `none`) | N — price is pool-verified (NOK 84.96, 2026-07-17) | — | Not applicable |
| No consensus / forward estimates | N — consensus present through FY2030E | — | Not applicable |
| No peer data | N — 10-company comp set present, as-of 2026-07-18 | — | Not applicable |
| Only one valuation method usable | N — five methods ran (own-history, peer, DCF, reverse-DCF, SOTP) | — | Not applicable |
| No cash flow AND DCF is only method | N — cash flow statement present and DCF is one of three weighted methods | — | Not applicable |
| SOTP not possible for multi-segment | N — SOTP ran fully (5 reportable segments, no >85% single-segment threshold) | — | Not applicable |
| Methods disagree >40% unreconciled | N — weighted base-case spread is 33.6% (below the 40% threshold), and it is explicitly reconciled in §3 | — | Not applicable |
| Terminal value >75% of DCF EV | **Y** — DCF terminal value is 78.1% of DCF EV [`04_intrinsic-dcf.md` §5] | Valuation confidence | Max 60 |
| Misaligned controlling owner (RF-OWN-004, §24 Filter 6) | **Y** — Norwegian State's 34.49% stake held for industrial-policy reasons, not per-share value; Board declined takeover-bid-handling principles because of it [`management-governance/99_management-governance-synthesis.md`, RF-OWN-004] | Valuation attractiveness; verdict ceiling | Attractiveness max 60 (actual read, 38, is already under this ceiling); value-trap flag mandatory (applied throughout §1–§7); verdict may not be better than "Modestly undervalued" on a cheap multiple alone (moot here — the verdict is "Fairly valued," not an undervalued call driven by a cheap multiple) |

No other caps bind. Where multiple caps could affect the same score, the terminal-dominance cap (max 60) is the binding, most restrictive constraint on valuation confidence; the final confidence score of 56 sits under that cap.

## 5. Fair-Value Summary

The bull/base/bear fair-value levels are NOK 107.70 / NOK 81.83 / NOK 45.12, with sum-of-the-parts the single method driving the base — it is the only one of the three weighted methods tied to audited, segment-level disclosures rather than a forecast or a discretionary discount, and it lands within 0.3% of the consolidated enterprise-value bridge. The current price (NOK 84.96) implies the market needs Hydro's FY2025 actual Adjusted EBITDA margin (13.9%) to hold roughly flat rather than fade toward the DCF's conservative 13.0% mid-cycle anchor — achievable in the sense that it does not require the current Middle East supply-shock aluminium-price spike to persist in full, but a real stretch given two earnings-module reads independently call the current elevated margin non-durable and the company's own forward hedge book already prices in partial reversion. The margin of safety is negative (−3.83% — price sits above, not below, base fair value), while the downside to the bear case is a real 46.89% — these are two separate reads, and together they describe an asymmetric setup (26.8% upside to bull vs 46.9% downside to bear) rather than a cushioned entry point. Any apparent cheapness in the peer-relative read (NOK 93.70 base, +10.2% vs price, or the wider 18%–35% discount on clean multiples before the quality adjustment) carries genuine value-trap risk: the business-model module scores Hydro's moat as narrow and eroding (Extrusions EBIT margin −2.2% in 2025, upstream cost-curve advantage exposed to Chinese/Gulf capacity growth), and the Norwegian State's 34.49% stake is held for industrial-policy reasons with no mandate to close a valuation gap — a structurally misaligned owner (RF-OWN-004) under which persistent cheapness does not self-correct.

## 6. What Would Change The Valuation Verdict?

| Current Verdict | What Would Make It Cheaper | What Would Make It More Expensive | Data Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fairly valued | Adjusted EBITDA margin confirmed fading toward the DCF's 13.0% mid-cycle anchor (or the FY2023 trough of 11.5%) while price does not correct in advance — would push the base case (SOTP/DCF-weighted) further below price and open a real margin of safety; evidence that the Extrusions restructuring (five plant closures) is delivering ahead of plan would also lift SOTP's Extrusions segment multiple range off its low end | Confirmation that the Middle East supply-shock aluminium-price premium persists structurally (e.g., a durable Strait of Hormuz-related supply curtailment) — this would validate the reverse-DCF's implied 13.9%–14.0% margin ask and pull the DCF and peer base cases up toward the SOTP/Bull range; a formal Board statement on takeover-bid-handling principles or evidence the Norwegian State supports value-accretive action would also remove the RF-OWN-004 attractiveness cap | Q2 2026 results (due 2026-07-22, three days after this run) — the first read on whether the Q1 2026 margin spike is fading toward `04`'s anchor or persisting; a longer (3-year) own-history multiple series to make `02`'s reversion read decision-relevant; a disclosed dilution schedule for the founder/subscription certificates |

## 7. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- Bull/base/bear fair-value levels: NOK 107.70 / NOK 81.83 / NOK 45.12 per share. Sum-of-the-parts (40% weight) is the dominant method — audited segment data, ties within 0.3% of consolidated EV.
- The price implies Hydro's FY2025 actual margin (13.9%) holds flat, not growth (implied FCF CAGR −3.21%) — a "Stretch, tilting aggressive" ask per the reverse-DCF, achievable only if the current cyclically-elevated pricing environment does not fully normalize.
- Margin of safety: **−3.83%** (no cushion — price sits above base fair value). Downside to bear: **46.89%** (bear-case value NOK 45.12). These are separate reads: modest apparent overvaluation on the base case, paired with a large asymmetric downside if the structural (not merely cyclical) moat-erosion case plays out.
- This is genuine value-trap risk, not a clean margin-of-safety opportunity: the peer-relative method's apparent 18%–35% discount on clean multiples is only partly explained by fundamentals (shrinking revenue, narrow/eroding moat) and is capped by RF-OWN-004 — the Norwegian State's 34.49% stake is held for industrial-policy reasons (retaining HQ/technology functions in Norway), not per-share value maximization, and the Board has declined to adopt takeover-bid-handling principles because of the stake's size. Persistent cheapness under this owner does not self-correct.
- Trust sum-of-the-parts most (audited segment data, tightest reconciliation to consolidated EV); trust the DCF second (mandated primary method for this business type, but terminal-dominated at 78.1% of EV); discount the peer-relative base case somewhat (it stacks a discretionary FX conversion and a discretionary quality discount); do not use the own-history multiples reversion figures as a fair-value input at all (13-month history, explicitly zero-weighted).
- No partial-data caps bind on the price/margin-of-safety/downside reads — the price is pool-verified and fresh (2 calendar days old). The only cap applied is the terminal-dominance cap on valuation confidence (max 60, DCF terminal value = 78.1% of EV) and the RF-OWN-004 attractiveness cap (max 60, non-binding given the actual read of 38).
- Biggest missing data point (single highest-value next data request): Q2 2026 results, due 2026-07-22 (three days after this run) — the first hard evidence on whether the Q1 2026 margin spike this whole valuation pivots on is fading toward the DCF's 13.0% mid-cycle anchor or persisting toward the price-implied 13.9%–14.0% level.
- **Explicit handoff:** the master synthesizer's "Valuation and Peer Mispricing" section should defer to this synthesis. The bull/base/bear fair-value levels here (NOK 107.70 / 81.83 / 45.12) are the inputs for the master's probability-weighted scenario model — this module does not assign probabilities, compute a probability-weighted return, or issue a rating.

## 8. Simple Summary

- Not cheap: the base-case fair value (NOK 81.83) is 3.7% *below* the current price (NOK 84.96) — fairly valued, no margin of safety.
- Bull NOK 107.70 (+26.8%) / Base NOK 81.83 (−3.7%) / Bear NOK 45.12 (−46.9%, structural, not just cyclical).
- The market is pricing Hydro's current elevated margin (13.9%) to hold flat, not to grow — a real but not extreme stretch.
- The downside sits in a structural moat-erosion case (Extrusions decline, upstream cost-curve pressure from Chinese/Gulf capacity) — 46.9% below today's price if it plays out.
- Trust sum-of-the-parts most for this company — it's built on audited segment data and matches the consolidated enterprise value almost exactly.
- Value-trap risk is real: the Norwegian State's 34.5% stake is held for industrial-policy, not per-share-value, reasons, so any apparent discount may never close.
- A pool-verified current price was available (NOK 84.96, 2026-07-17) — no price gap here.
- This module is useful for the master synthesizer: five methods ran, are reconciled, and produce a coherent, evidence-cited fair-value range with an explicit asymmetric-risk read.

The export itself timestamps the quote ("Share Price as of Jul-17-2026") — this is a true quote as-of date, not merely a file-download date (the export's own creation stamp, "Date Created: Jul-18-2026," is one day later and is the vendor's compile date, not the price date). No web price was needed or used.

Note: Capital IQ's separate "Historical Capitalization" tab links a different price (NOK 103.45) to the Mar-31-2026 balance-sheet date, dated "pricing as of" the Q1 2026 filing date (2026-04-29) — that is a filing-date-linked historical snapshot, not the current price, and is not used here. ## 4. Enterprise Value Bridge

Balance-sheet items below are as of Mar-31-2026 (Q1 2026), the latest available balance sheet — paired with the current price (2026-07-17). Norsk Hydro's Q2 2026 results are due 2026-07-22.

| + Minority / non-controlling interest | 7,495 | Capital IQ Balance Sheet tab, "Minority Interest," Mar-31-2026; Q1 2026 report balance sheet |
| + Preferred equity | 0 (none outstanding) | Capital IQ Capital Structure tabs — "Pref. Equity: —" |
| + Operating lease liabilities (separate add) | Not applicable — already inside Total Debt | See note above |
| + Underfunded pension / other long-term obligations | Not added (see below) | — |
| − Cash & equivalents (+ ST investments) — **headline / vendor basis** | (20,664) | Capital IQ Balance Sheet tab: Cash and Equivalents 11,251 + Short Term Investments 9,413 = 20,664, Mar-31-2026; Q1 2026 report balance sheet |
| **= Enterprise value (EV) — headline** | **187,555** | Formula above; matches Capital IQ's own precomputed TEV of NOK 187,555.05 mm |

**Cash quality — a materially different, more conservative EV.** The headline NOK 20,664mm "cash & ST investments" line nets in two blocks the company itself says are not freely available to service group debt:
- **NOK 1,390mm** held in Norsk Hydro's captive insurance subsidiary, Industriforsikring AS. The company's own words: "Cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments in Hydro's captive insurance company... are assumed to not be available to service or repay future Hydro debt, and are therefore excluded from the measure adjusted net debt." [Q1 2026 report, "Adjusted net debt" note, footnote 3]
- **NOK 3,439mm** posted as collateral for short-term and long-term liabilities — restricted, mainly tied to derivatives used for risk management. [Q1 2026 report, "Adjusted net debt" note, footnote 2]

Netting only the freely available balance (20,664 − 1,390 − 3,439 = **NOK 15,835mm**) gives:

| Component | Amount (NOK mm) |
|---|---:|
| Market capitalization | 166,970 |
| + Total debt | 33,754 |
| + Minority interest | 7,495 |
| − Cash quality-adjusted (freely available cash & ST investments) | (15,835) |
| **= Enterprise value — cash-quality adjusted** | **192,384** |

**This cash-quality-adjusted EV (NOK 192,384 million) is the canonical figure for this report**, per the conservative default (CLAUDE.md §4/§6): the captive-insurance balance and the derivatives-collateral balance are not cash the group could use to pay down debt, by the company's own admission, so treating them as ordinary netting cash understates EV by roughly NOK 4,829 million (~2.6% of the headline EV) and flatters net debt by the same amount. The headline vendor figure (NOK 187,555 million) is shown alongside because it is what Capital IQ and most screens will display by default — downstream agents should use the NOK 192,384 million adjusted figure unless they have a specific reason to prefer the headline.

**Adjustments NOT made:**
- **Pension:** Norsk Hydro carries a Pension & Other Post-Retirement Benefits liability of NOK 8,496mm (Mar-31-2026, already inside Total Liabilities) and separately discloses a "Net pension asset (obligation) at fair value, net of expected tax benefit" of +NOK 1,373mm in its own "Adjusted net debt" APM — i.e., the company treats its pension position as broadly funded, not a material debt-like add-on. This report does not add pension obligations to the EV bridge; the balance-sheet pension liability is already captured inside standard liabilities, not inside "Total Debt."
- **Equity-method investments:** NOK 21,654mm of long-term/equity-method investments (Mar-31-2026) — including Hydro's stake in the Qatalum smelter joint venture — sit inside total assets and are not netted separately from EV here. These are operating joint ventures integral to segment economics (reported within the Hydro Aluminium Metal segment), not passive financial holdings, so following Capital IQ's own treatment, they are left inside the consolidated asset base rather than carved out.
- **Contingent liabilities / other provisions:** not added; no separate quantified contingent-liability figure was identified as EV-bridge-relevant in this pass.
